Dolly Parton, the country music icon whose soaring vibrato vocals, poignant songwriting and sparkling costumes defined her rise from a log cabin in the Tennessee mountains to the height of stardom and acclaim, has died. She was 80 years old.

Known for her curvy physique, massive blonde wigs and skin-tight outfits that served her self-deprecating wit, she was among the most beloved personalities in music and beyond — the rare celebrity whose appeal transcended generations, geography and politics.

She wrote hundreds of songs, including classics like “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors” and “I Will Always Love You,” that totaled more than 100 million worldwide sales and more than 1 billion online streams. Parton, who plucked bejeweled banjos, guitar and dulcimers with her long fingernails during performances, was a generous philanthropist and successful businesswoman whose projects included a theme park in the Smoky Mountain foothills near her birthplace.

Her career was forever influenced by her upbringing as one of 12 children born into what she called a “dirt poor” Tennessee family. She started her education nonprofit, Imagination Library, to send free books to children in Tennessee because her father, who quit school to work on the farm, struggled to learn to read.

Parton's first musical performances were in church, where her grandfather was a preacher. By age 10, she was learning guitar and singing on local television shows. At 13, she appeared on the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville, where Johnny Cash introduced her as “a little girl here from up in East Tennessee.”

With a suitcase of songs, she followed her uncle, Bill Owens, also a songwriter, to Nashville after graduating high school in 1964. Fred Foster, who produced Roy Orbison, Willie Nelson and more, saw her potential and got her songs cut by other artists, as well as recording and releasing Parton singing her own material. By the mid-1970s, Parton was a Nashville queen.

A key collaboration with Porter Wagoner

Parton's partnership with Porter Wagoner, a pencil-thin pompadoured star with flashy rhinestone outfits, was key to her career. She honed her acting skills on his syndicated TV show and he advocated for her to get a record deal at RCA. Their first duet, “The Last Thing On My Mind,” was released in 1967, the same year she started her own publishing company.

While their duets were often big radio hits, Parton's solo singles didn’t chart as high at first. With Wagoner as a co-producer, she began to adjust her country warble to a more polished, pop-leaning style.

She got her first No. 1 solo single with “Joshua,” and reached the Top 5 with the ballad “Coat of Many Colors,” about how her mother sewed together scraps of clothes to make a coat Parton wore “so proudly” even as her peers mocked her for being poor. The song, with its Biblical references and ode to maternal love, was later made into a children’s book and a TV movie.

In 1973, she had the hit that made her career — “Jolene,” a country music standard with its steady, churning rhythm and Parton's repeated delivery of the title as she pleads for the woman not to steal her man.

The song topped the country charts, crossing over to pop and later being released internationally, opening up new audiences for Parton. “Jolene” is one of her most covered compositions, including by Miley Cyrus (Parton’s goddaughter), Olivia Newton-John and The White Stripes.

She left Wagoner’s show in 1974, amid reports of squabbling between the two, although they continued to record together and Wagoner stayed her producer for years after that. But the relationship turned litigious when Wagoner sued her in 1979 for millions in management fees and royalties.

A pop crossover star

She followed “Jolene” with a huge hit in 1974, “I Will Always Love You,” an ode and farewell to Wagoner that helped her win the Country Music Association’s female vocalist of the year back-to-back in 1975 and 1976. She famously turned down Elvis Presley, who wanted to record it, because she would not share publishing rights.

Decades later, Whitney Houston’s version of “I Will Always Love You” became a smash for the soundtrack of her 1992 film “The Bodyguard,” and broke sales records. Houston won a Grammy for her performance in 1994, presented to her by Parton.

“Here You Come Again,” a pop crossover hit and one of the few she didn’t write, further established Parton as a multi-genre entertainer and brought her first Grammy Award in 1979.

“A lot of people thought I had totally lost my mind,” she told The Associated Press in 1979 of changing her singing style. “But I had no fear of change. I expected success, but I was braced for failure. I didn’t care if people thought I was wrong. In my own heart, I knew I was doing the right thing.”

Parton's other crossover hits included the title song from “9 to 5,” the 1980 comedy starring Parton, Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin; and her duet with longtime friend Kenny Rogers, “Islands in the Stream,” written by brothers Barry, Maurice and Robin Gibb of the Bee Gees. In 1987, she collaborated with Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris on the million-selling “Trio” album.

Down home charm

For millions of fans, she was simply “Dolly,” a mixture of Southern charm, humor and glamour. But she was also considered a feminist role model for holding the reins of her own career, writing her own songs, owning her content and looking after her finances in an entertainment world dominated by men.

Parton was open to making fun of herself; when she hosted “Saturday Night Live” in 1989 she told the writers that her only restrictions were she wouldn’t curse and she wouldn’t make fun of Jesus. She regularly joked about her breasts or her dumb blonde appearance, but with a wink that she was the one controlling the laughs. In the memoir “My Life So Far,” Fonda remembered Parton's way with a wisecrack, “usually high raunch,” and a laugh that was “somewhere between a girl's giggle, an explosive shriek, and a cascade of little bells."

After her gown split down the front when she won CMA's entertainer of the year in 1978, Parton quipped: “My Daddy said that's what I got for putting 50 pounds of mud in a five-pound bag.”

Throughout her career, she embraced her glamorous style, often wearing custom curve-hugging rhinestone dresses and bodysuits even if they drew tsk-tsks from others in the industry. Her look was always a part of her larger musical business plan.

“I knew my songs were good even if I had been ugly as sin,” she told the AP in 2014. “So I thought, ‘Well, I would have probably chose to look this way even if I had been a waitress.’ I mean, this is my look. I mean, I like a lot of makeup. I like a lot of hair. I like flashy clothes. I like to show it off. But that’s just who I am.”

She married Carl Dean, an asphalt paving contractor, in the mid-1960s; they were together until his death in 2025 at the age of 82. Though rarely seen in public, he was an influence on her career. She told NPR that she wrote “Jolene” about a flirty bank teller who seemed to take an interest in Dean.

‘9 to 5’ to Hollywood and Broadway

In her first major film role, Parton played alongside Fonda and Tomlin as office workers who rebel against their tyrannical boss in “9 to 5.” Critic Roger Ebert called her a “natural-born movie star” and the title song earned her two Grammy Awards and a ranking of 78 on the American Film Institute's list of top 100 movie songs. Starring roles in the “The Best Little Whorehouse In Texas” and “Steel Magnolias” followed.

"I never thought of myself as a movie star," she told AP’s Bob Thomas in 1979. "I knew I'd be a star, but as a singer or as a writer of songs or books or poetry. I wanted to be a famous performer and wear flashy clothes, but singing in movies was not one of my ambitions. My family lived in the mountains and we didn't see movies.”

Her love affair with TV and film continued for decades, with appearances alongside Cyrus on “Hannah Montana” and adaptions of her music for Christmas specials, films and streaming series. She also became an author, her books ranging from the memoir “Dolly” to a bestselling novel co-authored by James Patterson, “Run, Rose, Run,"

The stage adaptation “9 to 5: The Musical” debuted in 2009, and “DOLLY: A True Original Musical” had been set to open in December 2026.

United States of Dolly

Beyond her music, Parton’s most lasting legacy might be her generosity and broad appeal.

When a deadly wildfire swept through the Smokies in 2016, she held an all-star telethon and set up a foundation that sent monthly checks to residents whose homes were damaged or destroyed.

She opened up her Dollywood theme park in East Tennessee, a major economic driver in Appalachia that draws tourists from around the country, and established the Dollywood Foundation. She wrote books and memoirs, was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame and was given a lifetime achievement award by the Recording Academy. She was selected for the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in 2025.

With 55 Grammy nominations and 10 wins, Parton is the third-most nominated woman in Grammy history, only behind Beyoncé and Taylor Swift.

Parton spanned social and political divides, through multiple generations of fans, urban and rural and in between. In tumultuous election years, it wasn't uncommon to see “Dolly for President” shirts. But she was strict in not voicing her own political beliefs, often turning aside questions about presidents, candidates, policies and other controversies.

“I don’t do politics," Parton told host Jad Abumrad on his hit podcast “Dolly Parton's America."

"I have too many fans on both sides of the fence. Of course, I have my opinion about everything, but I learned years ago to keep your mouth shut about things.”

When the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Foundation sent out a ballot in 2022 with her name on it, though she said she felt she hadn't earned it, the voters answered with a “Hello, Dolly." Parton showed up to the induction ceremony, performed and then put out a rock album.

___

Associated Press writer Hillel Italie contributed.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Newcastle cult hero, 34, appointed as club’s new loans manager and immediately tasked with flogging four players
Sports.content:
PAUL Dummett has been appointed as Newcastle United’s new loans manager.

The 34-year-old Premier League cult hero has already been tasked with sending four players away on loan for the 2026-27 season.



Former defender Dummett has joined the Magpies‘ loans department in his first executive role after announcing his retirement from professional football in December 2025.

It comes after ex-Newcastle striker Shola Ameobi, 44, was moved to become the team’s head of corporate affairs, according to The i Paper.



A restructure of the team’s loans department has also seen Peter Rampage, 42, take over as the talent management lead.

Right-back Leo Shahar and striker Sean Neave, both 19, are expected to be sent away on loan after attention from Championship and League One teams.

The former defender made 196 appearances for the Magpies between 2010 and 2024.

He was also sent on loan to Gateshead and St Mirren early on in his career, with later permanent moves to Wigan Athletic and Carlisle United.

Dummett was seen watching on as several young players were given vital experience during pre-season friendlies.

It is hoped that Newcastle’s revamped loans department can help close the gap between the club’s academy and first team.



The Magpies are continuing to spend big as the 2026-27 season swings into action with Nico Gonzalez, 24, set for a £50 million move from Manchester City.

Additionally, loan deals have been agreed for youngsters Antonio Cordero, Anthony Munda, both 19, and Alex Murphy, 22.

Newcastle opened their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-2 draw against Liverpool.

They will next travel south to face Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, August 29.

Sports.title: Inside Cole Palmer’s amazing lifestyle, from £4.3million Surrey mansion to influencer girlfriend and Burberry contract
Sports.content:
WHAT a difference a summer off makes.

Cole Palmer put on a masterclass for Chelsea on Monday Night Football, scoring and grabbing an assist in a 3-2 win over Fulham.





That came after he was cruelly snubbed by Thomas Tuchel for England’s World Cup squad.

But, instead of wallowing in self-pity, the Blues playmaker enjoyed some downtime with pals in Ibiza, where he was spotted partying with Wayne Lineker at his Ocean Beach club.

And that’s just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to Palmer’s amazing lifestyle off the pitch.

He lives in a stunning £4.3million mansion in Surrey, dates a beautiful influencer, and even caught the eye of fashion giants Burberry, who signed him up on a modelling contract.

There’s absolutely nothing ‘Cold’ about his existence.

Mansion fit for a king

Like many Chelsea footballers, Cole 24, resides in the leafy Surrey Village of Oxshott.

His home, worth £4.3million, is situated behind private gated grounds.

It boasts six bedrooms, an expansive entrance hall and living room, as well as a modern kitchen and dining room.





While there’s also an entertainment room, where he can play video games and relax with friends after playing football.

Although his planning application to build an outdoor gym sparked objections from his neighbours.

Influencer Wag

Cole is currently dating the stunning blonde model and influencer, Olivia Holder, dubbed the ‘Pilates Princess’.

They were first spotted together last December enjoying a date at London’s Winter Wonderland.

The 24-year-old stunner reportedly runs a beauty clinic alongside her sister in Bromley in Greater London.

A devout Christian, Olivia regularly discusses her faith on Instagram.

She is becoming the ultimate Chelsea Wag, and is often seen in the hospitality section at Stamford Bridge.

Olivia has enjoyed the trappings of Cole’s lifestyle, including luxury holidays in Dubai, Ibiza, Cannes, and Marbella.



Cars

When it comes to motors, Cole has a very impressive collection.

When he began life as a Man City trainee, his trusted car was a Volkswagen Polo.

But, now on a salary of £130,000-per-week, he’s been able to branch out to more luxurious brands.

The most impressive is his Lamborghini Urus, worth a whopping £190,000. It was customized by WRAPvehicles with neon green brake calipers and gloss black wheels.



He has added a BMW i4 M50 to his garage, worth around £72,000.

Cole also was seen behind the wheel of a reliable Mercedes-Benz A-Class, which starts at £31,000.

He’s in fashion

Thanks to his persona on the pitch, earning him the nickname ‘Cold Palmer’ because of his epic goal celebration, the midfielder has scored plenty of fans.

And many have taken to his fashion style too, dubbing it Palmercore – mixing high-street luxury brands with streetwear and tracksuits.

That said, he has rocked up to high-profile ceremonies like the PFA Awards and GQ Men of the Year events in designer suits and tuxedos, so he’s not always so paired down.

His style caught the attention of British fashion house Burberry, who signed him up on a seasonal campaign deal.

Cole went viral with a nine-minute fishing film for the brand called The Duffle with Cole Palmer.

Amusingly, the clip sees him sitting by a lake fishing in complete silence for the entire duration.



The playmaker also starred alongside Arsenal star Eberechi Eze for their It’s Always Burberry Weather campaign, where he wore Burberry’s classic coats and trademark knits.

Back in June, Cole was a cover star for trendy i-D Magazine in partnership with Burberry to model their latest collection.

There’s more to come…

All of this is brewing quite nicely to build Palmer into a brand.

Last October, Cole successfully trademarked the term ‘Cold Palmer’ with the UK government’s Intellectual Property Office.

What does that mean? Well, now no one can use his nickname for commercial purposes without first getting his permission first.

Second, he can now add that trademarked term to products he wants to endorse.

Think toys, clothes, footballs, football boots, and even food.

He also managed to trademark his name, autograph, and shivering goal celebration.



There is already a partnership with Gopuff who launched a premium ice brand they’ve aptly called COLE’D.

Expect more merch to follow.

Sports.title: Why Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa transfer is so complicated despite Chelsea outcast and Emery being perfect match
Sports.content:
NICOLAS JACKSON going to Aston Villa would make sense for everyone.

Chelsea want him off their books, Villa need a striker, and Jackson and Unai Emery would love to be reunited after their spell together at Villarreal.



But multiple factors, from Uefa’s “45-day rule” and Premier League loan regulations, to the intrigue surrounding Julian Alvarez’s future at Atletico Madrid, are putting spanners in the works.

Which is why Villa, after shadowing Jackson most of the summer, are now looking at other options, such as Crystal Palace’s wantaway frontman Jean-Philippe Mateta.



And why Chelsea, for the second summer in a row, find themselves scrambling to find Jackson a new home, preferably a permanent one.

Despite the fact the Senegal striker would be a more natural replacement for Ollie Watkins, if he joins the Villa exodus, than Mateta.



Chelsea and Villa have already done business this summer. Morgan Rogers moved to Stamford Bridge for £117m, a record for a British player, in late July.

Soon afterwards, Alejandro Garnacho moved in the other direction, on loan with a conditional buy clause.

But those deals make a Jackson move more difficult and less attractive for both clubs.

Under Uefa rules, if clubs sell players to each other within a 45-day period they are treated as a player swap – not as two separate transactions.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In those circumstances, the clubs are not able to put any profit on the player they have sold directly on to their books for accounting purposes.

The rules are complex, but the upshot is the selling clubs cannot enjoy the full benefit of the agreed fee when it comes to calculations related to Uefa and PL financial rules.

Rogers’ transfer to Chelsea was confirmed on July 21. So if Jackson were to move in the other direction before the window closes next Tuesday, the deal would fall within the 45-day window.

The result would be Villa not being able to add all the profit on Rogers to their accounts and Chelsea facing the same restriction on what they received for Jackson.



The Uefa regulations allow wriggle room if players move initially on loan, although there are still restrictions.

But that option is not open to Chelsea and Villa. PL rules say clubs can only have one player on loan from another PL club at any one time. And Garnacho is already filling that slot at Villa Park.

An added complication is Villa and Chelsea are already in Uefa’s bad books for breaching regulations.

They are operating under settlement agreements which set them financial targets they must meet to avoid further fines and punishment.



Villa have already sold Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa to help balance the books. Ollie Watkins wants to follow them out by making a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia.

Jackson would be much more of a direct replacement for Watkins than a player like Mateta.

Although Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, they still have to meet most of the terms of their settlement.

The Blues seem to be pretty cool right now about the Jackson situation, because of interest from other clubs. But Atletico seem like the best bet.



The LaLiga side have been in talks with the Blues on and off the whole summer.

Director of football Mateu Alemany was in London earlier this month.

But Atletico have, until now, been pushing for an initial loan deal for Jackson.

And Chelsea, after another busy summer of incomings, would much prefer a permanent deal.



They value the 25-year-old at £65m. Jackson arrived three years ago for £30m on an eight-year contract.

Which means his current value for accounting purposes, after allowing for amortisation, is just under £20m. So a £65m fee would bring a profit of more than £45m.

The trick will be finding someone willing to pay that much, either up front or as a compulsory purchase after an initial loan.

Atletico have so far resisted. But their own problems with Alvarez are coming to a head.



The Argentinian star has been pushing for a move, preferably to Barcelona, all summer.

The start of the new season has upped the stakes, with Alvarez being booed by Atletico fans and a toxic atmosphere developing.

It would be a major climbdown by Atletico if they sold their star player, after insisting he would be staying.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They were already looking at Jackson because of an injury to Alexander Sorloth. But if Alvarez left, the need for reinforcements up front on a longer-term basis would become critical.

All of which leaves Jackson in limbo, waiting to see if all the different rules and all the other transfer sagas will align for him to get his move away.

Sports.title: Man Utd CONFIRM £70million Carlos Baleba transfer from Brighton as Seagulls insert genius contract clause
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have announced the £70million signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, has penned a five-year deal at Old Trafford with the option of a further 12 months.



And his arrival for £65m plus £5m in add-ons should round off the Red Devils’ relentless midfield spending spree.

United bosses had already splurged £50m on Andrey Santos from Chelsea and £35m on Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.





But they wanted a third to sure up Michael Carrick‘s squad after Casemiro‘s move to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte‘s long-term knee injury.

And they teased the announcement with a tweet at 4.30pm on Tuesday.

The club simply wrote: “#areyouareabaleba” which sent United fans into ecstasy.

They then replied to their own post with a video of Baleba in the red home shirt saying: “Hi, I’m a Baleba.”



The official confirmation of the deal, including photos of the midfielder putting pen to paper, dropped at 4.45pm.

Baleba said: “It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick – his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”



Jason Wilcox, director of football, added: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further.

“He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

“Carlos’ determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.”

The fact the Red Devils have almost halved the £120m price tag they were quoted for Baleba last summer will come as some relief.



Brighton have covered their backs by inserting a sell-on clause which could bump up their earnings from the deal if United cash in down the line.

Last season was not the youngster’s finest on the South Coast as he managed only 35 goalless appearances in all competitions.

But United were long-standing admirers of Baleba, and they hope he can compete with Santos, Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo for the two deep-lying midfield spots in Carrick’s starting line-up.



The new recruit can also play at left-back, where United may need cover for Luke Shaw during a long season of domestic and European football.

Baleba has been nursing an ankle injury and is not expected to return until mid-September.

He scored four times in 112 appearances for Brighton after they snapped him up from Lille as a 19-year-old for £23.2m.

His last appearance for the Seagulls, ironically, came against Carrick’s United on the final day of last season.

Brighton sporting director Mike Cave said: “Carlos has made a significant contribution during his time with us and we’ve seen him develop both as a player and person here.



“When Carlos arrived, he was a young player with huge potential and, through his own hard work and commitment together with the support of our coaches and staff, he has developed into an outstanding Premier League midfielder.

“This is a move that Carlos was keen to make and we respect that he wants to take this opportunity at this stage of his career.

“We would like to thank him for everything he has done during his time at Brighton and wish him every success in the next chapter of his journey.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa set to complete stunning Leon Goretzka transfer as Champions League winner, 31, passes medical
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA are set to complete the signing of Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

And the Villans are also keen on recruiting Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta before next week’s transfer deadline.



Unai Emery‘s side are desperate to add to their squad following Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing at Brighton.

According to reporter Florian Plettenberg, the German international has completed his medical and will soon be announced as a Villa player.



Emery is said to have phoned Goretzka in a bid to convince him to join.

The former Bayern Munich star, 31, is expected to be pen a multi-year contract.



Goretzka had been a free agent since leaving Bayern at the end of last season.

The experienced midfielder remained a regular at Allianz Arena last season prior to his release, making 31 Bundesliga appearances and 48 in all competitions.

Goretzka signed for Bayern from Schalke in 2018 and played 312 times for the Bavarian giants, scoring 51 goals and laying on 53 assists.

He contributed to several trophy wins, including seven league titles and a Champions League.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Villa lost key midfielder Youri Tielemans to Manchester United last month, while Amadou Onana is set to be a long-term absentee with a knee injury.

Emery started Sunday’s thrashing at Brighton with Boubacar Kamara, Ross Barkley and Joao Gomes in midfield, the latter being sent off.

In addition to midfield, the Midlands club also want to bolster their forward line amid Ollie Watkins‘ mooted move to Saudi Arabia.

Earlier today it emerged that Villa have made an offer to sign Crystal Palace striker Mateta.



The bid is said to have been worth around £25million and was turned down by the Eagles.

Palace are claimed to want around £40m, despite Mateta’s contract being set to expire.

And the Villans are also considering swoops for Rafael Leao and Nicolas Jackson as the deadline approaches.

Sports.title: Arsenal strike transfer deal to sign wonderkid goalie, 15, with THREE more prodigies to come including Man Utd duo
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have continued their academy recruitment drive by agreeing a deal for Northern Ireland wonderkid Phoenix Blayney.

The goalkeeper, 15, will join the club next summer from Larne FC and be part of the Gunners’ scholarship intake for the 2027-28 season.



Blayney has also signed a pre-contract agreement to pen pro terms with Arsenal when he turns 17 in November next year.

The teenager has been tipped for a bright future and has already represented Northern Ireland at Under-17 level.



The Gunners have made a point of boosting their academy ranks with new signings to improve results.

The club are hoping to agree three more deals this week to bolster their Under-21 squad for the new season.

Manchester United duo James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye are set to arrive, as is Blackburn striker Igor Tyjon.

Work is also being done to bring in striker Vincent Joseph, 16, after he rejected the chance to pen pro terms with Liverpool.

Midfielder Axel Donczew, the youngest player to ever represent Cardiff, has already agreed to join the club.

And striker Mylo Bernard, who is also 16, is making his way to the Emirates after rejecting the opportunity to continue his development with Crystal Palace.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arsenal have made big changes to the academy this summer, with Pascal De Maesschalck now running the show.

The Belgian replaced Per Mertesacker, who left at the end of last season, and reports into sporting director Andrea Berta.

Sports.title: Chelsea legend QUITS England role after five years after landing ill-fated first role in management
Sports.content:
ASHLEY COLE has quit his England under-21 role after five years.

And SunSport understands he made the decision months before his ill-fated first job in management.



The Chelsea legend stepped down from his position with the young Lions in March before taking charge of Italian side Cesena.

The FA has now confirmed Cole will not return to his role with England.



His departure comes after the 45-year-old ended his short-lived spell as Cesena boss following just eight games in charge.

Cole landed his first managerial job with the Serie B club in March, having previously worked as part of the coaching staff at Everton and Derby.

But after just three months at the helm, he decided to walk away following discussions with Cesena’s sporting director over a change in the club’s strategy.

Cole announced his departure on Instagram.

He wrote: “As my tenure at Cesena FC concludes today, I want to thank the players and staff for their hard work and commitment over the last few months.

“I was proud to bring my experience to such a passionate club, and I’ve truly enjoyed working with the squad to introduce a new identity and prepare for the season ahead.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Following recent discussions with the Sporting Director regarding a change in the club’s strategy, I have decided that it is best for me to move on.

“I leave with great respect for all the people there, as well as the fans, and look forward to my next challenge.”

Cole signed a short-term contract with Cesena when he took over in March, with the option to extend if he met “certain conditions”.

But his first spell in management proved a major struggle.

He managed just one victory during his eight games in charge, alongside three draws and four defeats.



His appointment was met with a mixed reaction from Cesena supporters, while there were also reports of unrest among some players.

Cole also admitted he had struggled with the language barrier after moving to Italy.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea full-back had previously spent two years in Italy as a player with Roma, making 16 appearances for the club.

Cole made almost 400 Premier League appearances and won 107 England caps during a glittering playing career.

He also enjoyed two spells with Chelsea, winning multiple major trophies including the Champions League and Premier League.

Sports.title: Liverpool hold positive Barcola talks with optimism over deal with PSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool are holding further talks with Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday for Bradley Barcola.

There has been a gap in valuation between the two clubs throughout the summer, with PSG asking for around £145m for the France international.

However, those discussions have been described as positive and there is optimism that a deal can be struck.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains the four things Liverpool fans should know about transfer target Bradley Barcola

Sky Sports News understands there are good relations between the two clubs at the highest level. It is hoped this will help Liverpool and PSG reach an agreement.

Liverpool have also explored a move for Barcola's team-mate, Ibrahim Mbaye, who plays off the right wing.

The Premier League club's priority throughout this window has been to reinforce in wide areas.

They have been pursuing Barcola and Mbaye, while Brighton have also rejected two Liverpool offers for Yankuba Minteh, the latest being £60m.

Liverpool are currently the only club chasing Barcola, who has entered the final two years of his deal and has grown dissatisfied with his role at the European champions.

Liverpool, meanwhile, do not want to sell Cody Gakpo amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and would likely need two new wingers in before considering letting the Netherlands international go.

Sports.title: Littler's bid for historic PDC majors sweep suffers blow with PC27 exit
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's bid to qualify for the Players Championship Finals, and keep alive his hopes of claiming a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles in 2026, suffered a blow with a quarter-final exit at PC27.

Littler was beaten 6-5 by Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena in a final-leg decider in Leicester.

The world No 1 has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Image: Littler has won every PDC major title so far in 2026

Littler is left still needing to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals to achieve something no-one has ever managed in the sport.

The major obstacle standing in the 19-year-old's way, however, is that only the top 64 in the Players Championship Order of Merit make it through to the finals in Minehead in November.

Littler opted out of the first 26 events of the season before entering PC27 and 28 in Leicester, meaning he needs to have strong showings in the final few events to stand a chance of qualifying.

PC28 on Wednesday gives him another opportunity to claim a tournament win and boost his finals hopes.

Sports.title: Man Utd complete Baleba signing
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, joins the club in a deal worth up to £70m, made up of a £65m guaranteed fee plus £5m in add-ons.

He has signed a five-year contract which includes the option of a further year.

Baleba is currently injured, having picked up an ankle injury in pre-season, but Sky Sports News understands he could be back by mid-September. Manchester United play Manchester City on September 13, live on Sky Sports.

Baleba's arrival at Old Trafford brings an end to a transfer saga that has lasted almost 12 months. Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and becomes their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour," Baleba told the club's website.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and made 112 appearances for the club. He featured 35 times last season and was absent for a spell while representing Cameroon at the Africa Cup of Nations.

'I had no idea what this club would become' - Baleba pens Brighton farewell

Upon the announcement of the news, Baleba took to social media to post an emotional farewell to Brighton.

"I came here at 19 with little English and no idea what this club would become to me," he wrote.

"Brighton only asked me to be myself. The staff who make the club run so well. The team-mates who took the time to understand me, on the pitch and off it. The nights at the Amex when I heard my name from that stand always made me feel at home.

"To all of the fans, staff and my team-mates. You looked after me and for that I will hold you all close to my heart. Wherever I play, this club is in how I play. Good luck Seagulls."

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Sky Sports' William Bitibiri explains exactly what Carlos Baleba might bring to Manchester United's midfield

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Carlos Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Carlos Baleba's Premier League best bits

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes this a gamble for United. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

Image: Baleba was among the league's leading defensive midfielders during the 2024/25 season - can he revive that form?

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

Sports.title: PGA Tour: Tour Championship will be played in a match play format from 2028
Sports.content:
The PGA Tour has announced that the Tour Championship will be played in a two-week match play format as part of a new season-ending structure which will be implemented from the 2028 season.

It is one of a series of major schedule shake-ups coming to the PGA Tour, with the US circuit also set to introduce a new two-tier system which will feature promotion and relegation.

From 2028 onwards, the current series of FedExCup Playoffs, which are played in a stroke play format, will be replaced by:

A 72-hole stroke play PGA Tour Championship Series Finale featuring the top 90 golfers on the PGA Tour season-long points list

The top 32 players on the PGA Tour's points list at the end of the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale will qualify for the Tour Championship, a standalone two-week match play event

The match play tournament will be similar to the World Cup, with groups and knockouts

It will be the first time in the PGA Tour's history that the Tour Championship has been decided over a match play format, and is also the first time that the format has been played on the tour since the 2023 WGC Dell Technologies Match Play.

"Throughout this process, we listened carefully to our fans, players and partners," PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The PGA Tour revealed it would be introducing a new two-tier structure in 2028

"One message came through clearly: the culmination of our season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there.

"The result is a season-ending structure that rewards excellence over the course of the year while building toward a reimagined Tour Championship. We are creating something different, something distinct within professional golf that can resonate far beyond it."

How will the new PGA Tour postseason work?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said players will compete for season-long ranking points as usual, before the final standings are confirmed at the new PGA Tour Championship Series Finale

Throughout the 2028 season, players will compete to win points as normal throughout regular-season tour events, in a similar fashion to the current FedExCup system.

The season-long points race will then conclude at the new PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, a 72-hole stroke play event.

The top 90 players in the year-long points race rankings will compete at the event, which will confirm the season-ending points race leader and final rankings for the year.

After the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, the top 32 players in the year-end points rankings will then gain a place at the Tour Championship.

How will the new Tour Championship work?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The top 32 players in the season-long points rankings will feature at the revamped Tour Championship

The revamped Tour Championship will take place the week after the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, with a field of 32 players competing over a three-round group stage, akin to the FIFA World Cup.

Players will be seeded, depending on their standing in the final season-long points race list.

Each golfer will square off against the other players from their group, with the top two players in each group advancing to week two of the Tour Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The changes will revamp the current FedExCup Playoffs schedule

Should a tie take place following the end of the group stage, a play-off will occur.

Sixteen players will then advance to week two of the match play final, where the Tour Champion will be confirmed.

Players will then compete in a four-round match play competition. The final two undefeated players will duke it out for the title.

A player's record and final standings at the Tour Championship will be determined by their record throughout the two-week match play event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The winner across the two match play events will be crowned the Tour Champion

"Each week of the Tour Championship will be played at a different course," Rolapp added.

"This new format creates an exciting opportunity to showcase some of the most renowned venues in our sport, including places the modern tour has never been before."

Venues for the 2028 PGA Tour Championship Series Finale and Tour Championship will be confirmed in February 2027, with the US circuit explaining it will rotate hosting duties among "prestigious courses" and some venues the tour has not been able to feature in the past.

Sports.title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba has signed a five-year contract with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.

Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer when Casemiro left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.

“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-old a week ago.

United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Two goals, some polish and a rebrand: City flip Sávio for quite the profit
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN WINGERS UNDER THE HAMMER

We see Manchester City have managed to flip Savinho for quite the profit. Football Daily had previously assumed this sort of wheeler-dealing was restricted to the Dion-Dublin-adjacent property market, or the Harry-Redknapp-infused used car scene, but it seems we were mistaken. We have no idea how City ended up trousering a £44.2m markup on a player who cost £30.8m two seasons ago, and has achieved the square root of eff all since, but they’ve done it. Consider standing stock still and allowing a ball to clank off you and into the net in an FA Cup tie at Newcastle analogous to installing a new bathroom suite and giving the front room a lick of paint, or taking a microfibre cloth and some polish to the crevices of that grimy dashboard. Result! Goal! Ker-ching! That’s 75 million-nil!

Spurs were the mark, and they could end up paying £85m if all the silverware-related add-ons kick in. So £75m it is, then. But that’s still a fair old whack for an attacking player who scored two goals for City in 53 league appearances. The 22-year-old Brazilian plays on the right flank, so will almost certainly take the place of Mikey Moore, who thought his day at Brentford last weekend had gone badly enough, only for his manager Roberto De Zerbi to go out of his way to namecheck him – and him alone, twice – in his post-match deconstruction of a 3-0 fiasco for which pretty much everyone wearing Tottenham’s traditional blue, gold and dayglo pink was culpable.

Upon signing, Savinho announced that he wishes to be known forthwith as Sávio, reverting to the monicker from his time at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and set up 10 others during a loan stint that was a damn sight more successful than his spell at the Etihad. It’s also his actual name, so there is that. Sávio is far from the first of his countrymen to toy with this most personal of brands – Brazil’s greatest-ever player was actually called Manuel Francisco dos Santos, and Pelé was the result of a name change too – and we’re pretty sure he won’t be the last. Spurs meanwhile will simply be hoping they’re getting the Girona version of their new purchase, because otherwise City will have, in more ways than one, properly flipped them off. Omar Marmoush – 16 goals in 62 appearances, brand-new kitchen worktops, shiny hubcaps – next!

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
