Sports.title: Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day
Sports.content:
Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

Baleba has signed a five-year-contract at Old Trafford with the option to extend it by 12 months after agreeing personal terms and passing a medical.

United will pay an initial £65m and up to £5m more in add-ons to Brighton who have included a sell-on clause as part of the deal.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international, who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury, becomes United's third midfield signing of the summer after the club spent a total of £85m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba, who has been linked with United for more than a year, said: 'It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

'I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

Carlos Baleba has completed a £70million transfer to Manchester United from Brighton

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford, with the option for an extra year

'The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.'

United's director of football Jason Wilcox is delighted to complete the club's midfield rebuild after Casemiro left as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte was ruled out for much of this season with a knee ligament injury.

'Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further,' said Wilcox. 'He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

'We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

'Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.'

Fans will be relieved to see United get the deal over the line, particularly after their woeful start to the season at Hull City on Saturday.

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, both coming from set-pieces, left the Mancunians in the dust.

United's midfield of Santos and Tielemans with Fernandes ahead of them, lacked the dynamism that Baleba should hopefully aid with once he's fit.

Sports.title: Revealed: Chelsea's Spygate threat at Cobham HQ after two unknowns caught walking past training, Cristiano Ronaldo's set-piece analyst joins Blues and what really happened with Enzo Fernandez after Fulham win - CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL
Sports.content:
Revealed: Chelsea's Spygate threat at Cobham HQ after two unknowns caught walking past training, Cristiano Ronaldo's set-piece analyst joins Blues and what really happened with Enzo Fernandez after Fulham win - CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There is a secret entrance to Chelsea’s training ground. Those arriving via the nearby Cobham & Stoke D’Abernon train station use it frequently because it beats going the long way around.

Only regular visitors to the club’s Surrey HQ know it is there, this doorway which takes you down a passage surrounded by foliage until you are left walking towards the first-team building.

However, Willie Isa did not appear too pleased with the use of this hidden gate last week. The New Zealand-born former Samoa rugby league star, who is now Chelsea's player support and development officer on Xabi Alonso's staff, seemed irked that two unknowns had walked past what was supposed to be a closed training session on Friday.

Clubs are understandably cautious around unknown visitors to training grounds following the Southampton Spygate scandal earlier this year. As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Saints manager Tonda Eckert sent a junior analyst to record opposition training sessions, for which the club were kicked out of the Championship play-offs in May and docked four points from this season's campaign.

You can only get through the offending Cobham gate if security let you through after verifying your identity, so these individuals will have had clearance to be within the Cobham grounds on this particular afternoon. Yet Isa did not know who they were, and did not seem to like that they had potentially gotten a glimpse of Cole Palmer and Co preparing for their Premier League opener away at Fulham.

Let’s just say the security staff from then on were telling those trying to use this gate that they had better make the 15-minute walk to the front entrance – just as it began raining above Cobham.

Two unknown people were caught walking past Chelsea's closed training session at Cobham, sparking fears of a potential Spygate

Willie Isa (left), the former rugby league star who is now Chelsea's player support and development officer, has warned security not to let anyone in through the offending gate

Blues hire Ronaldo's set-piece analyst

After bringing in Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa, Chelsea have further added to their set-piece department by hiring a new first-team analyst called Andre Reis.

Reis spent the last seven years working with the Portuguese FA, analysing set-pieces for Portugal at the 2026 World Cup, throughout their victorious 2024-25 Nations League campaign and at Euro 2024.

Reis’ role was believed to involve on-pitch work as well as from behind his laptop. He built his way up to helping Cristiano Ronaldo and Co after originally acting as an analyst for Portugal’s youth.

Now, he will be helping Chelsea’s new set-piece specialist MacPhee, who joined this summer from Aston Villa and also spent the last year with Portugal.

Alonso said last week that he wants the ‘best possible specialists’ in every department.

Chelsea have brought in Andre Reis, who has been working with Portugal on set-pieces

Revealed: Hudson-Odoi's agent banned

Callum Hudson-Odoi’s brother, Bradley, who is the former Chelsea and current Nottingham Forest winger’s agent, has been suspended for six months.

Bradley was accused of breaching FA Rule E1.2, and charged with allegedly approaching or representing a minor without first obtaining the additional authorisation; and that he then performed agent services without first entering into a representation agreement.

The FA hit him with a six-month suspension from all activity that falls under the Football Agent Regulations, including but not limited to Football Agent Services. The ban began on Monday this week and it will end on February 24, 2027. He was also fined £500.

Callum, who joined Chelsea as a seven-year-old and went on to make 126 first-team appearances as well as being capped three times by England, signed a new contract with Forest last season which was overseen by his sibling. That deal ties him down to the City Ground until 2028. He was an unused substitute in their opening-day home defeat by Leeds United.

Confidential contacted Bradley for comment and received no reply.

Bradley Hudson-Odoi (right), brother of Callum, came through Fulham's academy and was a non-League forward for 10 years before retiring in 2019 and becoming an agent

Sources say, Liquidator will stay!

Stamford Bridge sources say they will not be following Wolverhampton Wanderers in binning their traditional pre-match playing of The Liquidator.

After a review, Wolves have confirmed the song will be avoided at Molineux, owing to supporters using its tune to chant offensively about their rivals, West Bromwich Albion.

Some Chelsea fans still use The Liquidator to sing ‘f*** off Tottenham’ at the Bridge, though much of the fanbase have been vocal in saying they do not like how a mention of Spurs invades what should be their song as the players prepare to play.

Chelsea’s first home fixture is against Luton Town on Thursday in the Carabao Cup with Brighton visiting in the Premier League on Sunday.

Enzo's full-time antics

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1, but those inside Stamford Bridge are also entitled to believe they hold the power over this situation.

Fernandez is tied down to a long-term deal, and as shown in Chelsea's Premier League opener away at Fulham, they are happy to keep using him.

They would only sell the Argentine for an enormous sum after spending all summer demanding at least £120million, and they want a replacement lined up. Otherwise, they would be weakening themselves and strengthening a rival.

A video clip on social media appeared to show Fernandez walking away from his Chelsea team-mates and towards the tunnel as they stood in front of the away end following their 3-2 Premier League victory over Fulham.

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1

However, Confidential was at Craven Cottage, and in his defence, Fernandez did stand in front of the visiting supporters with everyone else. We then watched as Fernandez gave his shirt to a fan in the home end – we think they were holding a River Plate away shirt if our eyes were not deceiving us, in homage to the team he joined as a six-year-old and represented for 15 years – before exiting.

The BBC’s Match of the Day title credits this season include Fernandez in his Chelsea shirt, shown briefly in between Xavi Simons for Tottenham Hotspur and Erling Haaland for City.

It is almost as if the Beeb are tempting fate after the Argentine's noisy ‘will he, won't he’ summer.

Anything can happen while the summer window remains open and City boss Enzo Maresca made a point of using Marc Guehi in midfield next to Elliot Anderson in their 2-1 comeback win over Bournemouth. Anderson left the field injured in the second half.

Neto asking price puts off Saudi bids

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto at close to £100million.

The Blues slapped that valuation on Neto after noting the asking prices for other wingers in this window and because they appreciate him highly internally.

However, Al Hilal are now getting closer to an agreement for Martinelli instead worth between £50-55million, with Neto relegated to a back-up option.

Neto got an earful from Chelsea captain Reece James during their 3-2 win at Fulham for not tracking back after he replaced Malo Gusto as a right wing-back.

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli (right) after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto (left) at close to £100million

Josh steps in and steps up

The Chelsea predicted lineup in Fulham's matchday programme had Wesley Fofana starting in the visitors’ defence despite being suspended for this clash.

In Fofana’s place, Josh Acheampong impressed, though the 20-year-old academy graduate's situation remains one to watch between now and the end of the window. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport last week, Chelsea have been considering whether to keep him where he is or sanction a loan.

They have long maintained that they do not want to sell him permanently. But performances like the one he put in at Fulham may only tell a few suitors that he is ready for more regular game time.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Joshua Zirkzee will leave United with Aston Villa and Serie A duo circling, why Amazon documentary is doubling stars' workload and how club have slashed Old Trafford beer queues this season
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee fully expects to leave Manchester United in the next week, Confidential understands.

While there is a feeling that United need more players through the door before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline following the shock opening-day defeat at newly promoted Hull City, there is an expectation that Zirkzee will go – most likely on loan.

A £36.5million signing from Bologna two years ago, Juventus have set their sights on taking Zirkzee back to Italy. There is interest from their Serie A rivals Napoli and Aston Villa have also enquired.

The 25-year-old Dutchman made just five starts in all competitions last season and was an unused substitute at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. Zirkzee is eager to get regular first-team minutes, and the sense around the player is that a compromise is required on all sides to facilitate a move.

Zirkzee is one of the most popular players in the dressing-room, but with his best position being as a No10 – the role occupied by captain Bruno Fernandes – opportunities to play are at a premium.

As for replacing Zirkzee, who has scored just nine times in 75 appearances for the club, United are prioritising a new left-back amid interest in Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and 19-year-old Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander. But insiders are far from certain there will be any more incomings to add to £155million midfield trio Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, and free-agent goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

Joshua Zirkzee is expected to leave Manchester United in the next week

After scoring on his United debut at home to Fulham two years ago, Zirkzee has added just eight more goals in 74 appearances

United announced the £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton on Tuesday but are not currently close to adding any more arrivals before the window closes next week

Double or Nothing!

Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary has doubled United’s broadcast commitments this season.

Filming began during the club’s pre-season camp in Dublin earlier this month and hit full flow last week, with crew working on the access-all-areas documentary now part of the furniture at Carrington and Old Trafford. The demands of producing the programme have dawned on those at a club which is already the biggest media draw in the Premier League for players and staff.

The Amazon documentary may be earning the club more than £10million, but it means United face twice the broadcasting demands as before, representing a real challenge in a season that could bring as many as 15 extra games following a return to Europe.

It’s understood that all the United stars have had to sign waivers giving permission to be filmed behind the scenes, and journalists covering the club have done likewise so that footage from Michael Carrick’s press conferences can be included.

MUTV’s studio boost

As much as Amazon are demanding a significant amount of United’s time, Confidential understands the new Snapdragon Studio at Carrington has been installed for the benefit of MUTV rather than the streaming giant.

The editing suite on the first floor of the training ground will be used by the club’s in-house TV station to produce the increasing amount of content United broadcast on their own channels. The equipment there is powered by Snapdragon as part of United’s £60million-a-year shirt sponsorship deal with California-based tech firm Qualcomm which is currently due to run until 2029.

Amazon will have to use their own facilities to produce the highly-anticipated docuseries on United which is due to air in the summer of 2027.

Sleeve it out

With Snapdragon on board as shirt sponsor for at least another three years, and Betway having recently agreed a record deal to have their name on United’s training kit, the club are now looking for a new sleeve sponsor.

United’s £20million-a-year partnership with DXC Technology ran out in May after four seasons, and they kicked off the new campaign at Hull on Saturday without branding on their sleeve for the first time in eight years.

The club were prepared to be patient last season when they went without a training-kit sponsor after the deal with Tezos lapsed, before cashing in on their return to the Champions League this season by signing the multi-year agreement with Betway. The deal, also believed to be worth £20m-a-year, is said to be the biggest standalone training kit or playing shirt sleeve deal in world football.

Reds escape rail chaos

United avoided the rail chaos that affected many of their 2,400 fans at Hull on Saturday by travelling back from Humberside on the team bus – although some players returned under their own steam.

United stars trudge off the pitch at the MKM Stadium after the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last Saturday

The Reds routinely take the train to games in London, and usually fly further afield, but the 200-mile round trip between Manchester and Hull meant that Carrick and his squad went there and back by bus.

It was just as well after the matchday announcer at the MKM Stadium appeared to take great pleasure in informing the United fans that the trains scheduled to depart from Hull for Manchester at 3.30pm and 5.03pm had been cancelled – much to the delight of the Hull supporters.

The team bus got away on time, but not before Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw were spotted walking across the car park towards their own transport. Confidential understands that several other United players did the same because they had plans for their day off on Sunday.

OT is pitch perfect

United may have requested to kick off the new season away from home so they could complete a major upgrade of the pitch at Old Trafford, but Confidential understands that the stadium would comfortably have been ready to host a game last weekend.

The turf has been relaid for the first time in 14 years – complete with new foundations and drainage system – and United have also taken steps to protect the players from injury by safeguarding the perimeter of the pitch.

The club confirmed earlier this summer that ‘the grass is being extended to provide a consistent surface at pitchside, and a layer of protection is being added to the brickwork at the foot of Old Trafford’s famous slope’.

There had been concerns over the ditch and perimeter wall that were created when the pitch was elevated in the 1990s, with players at risk of injury if they came off the grass at speed and collided with the advertising hoardings. Most recently, Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday.

United have also upgraded the home and away dugouts to increase the number of seats for substitutes and coaching staff from 16 to 20, in keeping with UEFA criteria ahead of the club’s return to the Champions League.

Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin after colliding with an advertising hoarding in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday

All the work was completed in advance of United’s trip to Humberside, meaning the club could have played at Old Trafford last weekend after all, although insiders say the extra week will give the new turf – which is made up of 96 per cent natural grass and four per cent artificial fibres – more time to mature before Sunday’s home opener against Ipswich Town.

United have made the improvements despite pressing ahead with plans to build a new stadium to replace Old Trafford, hopefully by 2035.

The club have also improved the stadium experience for fans as part of new partnership with Levy, the sports and entertainment hospitality specialists. It aims to provide a better quality, faster service for supporters which has seen new draught beer taps installed around Old Trafford. There will be more self-service bars which will enable fans to tap their payment card and grab a beer, which should reduce queues and improve flow.

There will also be a wider range of dining options outside the ground, including a number of kiosks featuring independent Manchester vendors selling street food.

JJ passes Under 21s audition

Confidential was in position at Leigh Sports Village on Monday night to witness JJ Gabriel’s stunning competitive debut for the Under 21s.

Gabriel, still only 15, scored a sublime goal when he chipped Ipswich Town goalkeeper Woody Williamson from outside the area, and also added two assists for Victor Musa and Jaydan Kamason.

Michael Carrick and his assistant Steve Holland were among the small crowd in Leigh, and it was hard not to marvel at Gabriel’s display as he thrived in a No10 role.

The Under-21s played in a 4-2-3-1 system to mirror the first team, even playing without a recognised No9, much like Carrick did at Hull by using Matheus Cunha through the middle. That allowed Gabriel to play the Bruno Fernandes role. The expectation is that Gabriel will train regularly with the first team throughout the season while also playing a starring role in the Under 21s.

JJ Gabriel, still only 15, scores a sublime chip from the edge of the area against Ipswich Town Under 21s

He scored 29 times across 32 appearances last season, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals

He was outstanding for the Under 18s under Darren Fletcher last season despite starting it as a 14-year-old. He scored 29 times across 32 appearances, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals.

Carrick and Holland were beaming by full time. With a star like Gabriel on their hands, who could blame them?

Scouts flock to see Under 21s

It was noticeable just how many EFL scouts were there on Monday night to watch an Under 21s team that is still ripe for picking before next week’s deadline.

Kamason and Harry Amass, who started at right-back and left-back in the 5-0 win, are both expected to draw interest. Confidential understands that both are expected to leave, with permanent exits not being ruled out as both players draw significant interest in the Championship, with nothing left for either to gain in academy football.

United have cashed in on several young players this summer as Radek Vitek, Tyler Fredricson and Ethan Williams left the club permanently, with buy-back clauses and matching rights included as part of their exit packages.

Jaydan Kamason celebrates scoring the third goal in United Under 21s' 5-0 win over Ipswich

Harry Amass, who started at left-back on Monday against Ipswich, is also likely to leave United in the next week

New cyber threat warning

News that Premier League teams face a fine of up to £100,000 if they fail to follow new cybersecurity rules coming into effect this season revived memories of the attack on United in November 2020, which paralysed the club’s computer network.

Staff were forced to communicate by WhatsApp for several weeks after the ransomware attack crippled United’s email accounts and other systems, forcing the club to call in the National Cyber Security Centre for help.

It was never revealed how much the hackers demanded as a ransom – or if United paid up – but the NCSC said at the time that the biggest single loss to a sports organisation from cyber-crime was £4million. United are believed to have upgraded their cybersecurity since then in an attempt to prevent another breach. The new rules will be implemented in three phases through April 2029.

Jamie Akhtar, CEO and co-founder of CyberSmart, said: ‘This is an important shift for the Premier League. Cyber security is moving from being viewed primarily as an IT responsibility to becoming an enforceable element of club governance.

‘Football clubs hold significant volumes of sensitive supporter, employee and player data, while also relying on systems for ticketing, payments, stadium access and matchday operations.’

Wes & Pally at Salford

Given that United host Ipswich Town on Sunday, those at a loose end on Saturday need look no further than Salford Lads & Girls Club.

United are teaming up with the iconic club to host an open day where former players Wes Brown and Gary Pallister will be in attendance. The pair are hosting a Q&A at the event which will give fans the chance to buy limited edition adidas third shirts, which have been designed to celebrate the Salford club’s centenary year.

A football fun day, which starts at midday, for those after a football fix on Saturday.

Sports.title: What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery, why he could still sign new contract and Villa's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins’ absence from the Aston Villa team for the opening-day thrashing at Brighton is the latest chapter in a story that started 18 months ago.

Manager Unai Emery was so enraged by his star striker's omission from the matchday squad on the south coast amid rumours of a move to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal that he could only reply 'silence' when asked what had caused it, adding: 'I think you can call him, call his agent and he can respond.'

The England forward spoke to his team-mates on Monday to explain his side of the story and was expected to return to some training this week. The stance remains the same: Villa are willing to sell Watkins to the Saudis, but only if their current valuation of at least £50million is matched.

That may shift in the days ahead, with Villa seeking reinforcements in defence, out wide and at centre-forward. Though this row might have been handled differently by both sides, it has not come from a clear blue sky.

Daily Mail Sport looks at how we got here and what might happen next.

Where it all began

At some point last week, Watkins had a discussion with Unai Emery. The Villa boss left those talks believing Watkins wanted to move to Al Hilal and was prepared to go to significant lengths to ensure the deal went through.

Unai Emery was in no mood to protect Ollie Watkins when his star striker was not available for the opening day at Brighton

Al Hilal, whose squad includes former Wolves captain Ruben Neves (furthest right) and Chelsea centre back Kalidou Koulibaly (second right) need to match Villa's £50m valuation

Watkins did not train last week as he waited for Villa to accept a bid. Al Hilal did not make the required offer and once he understood Watkins would not be involved in the preparation work, Emery did not consider him for last Sunday’s match at Brighton.

Without the injured Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, strikerless Villa were hammered 4-0 and Emery did nothing in his media appearances to protect Watkins. Sure enough, the 30-year-old was targeted mercilessly by supporters online.

To understand why this happened, we must rewind to a sliding doors moment for Villa and Watkins – Boxing Day 2024. In the previous three league games, Emery had decided to pick Jhon Duran, the chaotic but brilliant Colombian, ahead of Watkins, and Duran had scored in all three.

Heading into the next match at Newcastle, it looked as though Duran had become Villa’s undisputed No1 striker and the club started to make contingency plans for January. They knew Arsenal were chasing a forward and had an interest in Watkins, a boyhood Gunners fan.

Then Duran was given a straight red card at Newcastle and when he completed his suspension, Emery did not feel his form or attitude merited a return to the team. Al Nassr arrived with a £70million offer for Duran and Villa decided to cut their losses on a player who was hugely difficult to manage.

Villa were unwilling to sell both forwards in the same window and Watkins was denied his dream move to Arsenal, whose offers never approached Villa’s £65million valuation. The forward was disappointed but at the end of the window, Emery said: ‘Now we need him, like he needed Aston Villa.’

As far as the Spaniard is concerned, the same applies now. Emery has already lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa this summer and wants a few senior men to stick with him to build the new era, which includes another Champions League campaign this season.

Usually, Emery does not stand in a player’s way if he wants to depart but this one feels more personal.

Aston Villa have already lost the likes of Youri Tielemans (left) and Morgan Rogers (right) this summer and Watkins (centre) may be next

Jhon Duran was primed to be Villa's No1 striker 18 months ago before a red card at Newcastle

Contrasting positions

Watkins is easily the top client at Two Touch, the agency run by former Arsenal youngster Paolo Vernazza which represents an extensive list of players including Watkins’ Villa team-mate Matty Cash and Crystal Palace midfielder Will Hughes.

If Watkins were to move to Al Hilal, it would likely be one of Two Touch’s biggest deals and it is clear Villa are unhappy with how Vernazza has handled it. Vernazza may yet push this one through but were he to have his time again, he might make a different plan. Daily Mail Sport has attempted to contact Vernazza since Sunday but he has yet to respond.

Watkins is thought to earn a little more than £100,000 a week at Villa yet the salary proposed by Al Hilal is thought to be substantially more. Watkins has been Villa’s leading scorer in every season since he joined from Brentford in 2020 and is their all-time top Premier League marksman.

He has also seen Ezri Konsa, who is two years younger, allowed to join Arsenal for roughly the same sum Villa want from Al Hilal. Watkins turns 31 in December and if he believed Villa’s price was too high for a player his age, you could understand it. Not surprisingly, Villa see it differently.

Since Emery took charge in 2022, Watkins has developed into one of the best strikers in Europe, thanks also to Emery’s willingness to back him. Duran had to score five times after coming off the bench before he was given a run in the side. Donyell Malen was sold to Roma last January because Emery backed Watkins over the Dutchman, who has since scored 18 times in 21 games for the Serie A club.

Even when Watkins scored only once before December last season, and only once more between January 4 and March 11, Emery kept faith – and was rewarded when his main man hit 12 in 13 games at the end of the season to force his way into England’s World Cup squad.

Emery has lost four key players this summer and with two forwards injured, he felt he really needed Watkins at Brighton. No wonder he was ticking before the pre-match interviews. With Emery, the less he says, often the angrier he is.

He looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual, grew irritable with the opposing bench and stalked down the tunnel at full time without approaching Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler for a handshake. Emery and Hurzeler are certainly not best friends, but the reaction was still telling.

Emery looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual and grew irritable with the opposing bench

Watkins struck 12 goals in the final 13 games of last season to force his way into England's squad for the World Cup, where he scored in the warm-up against Costa Rica

Is there a way back?

A year ago, it looked as though Emiliano Martinez had played his final game for Villa. Desperate to move to Manchester United or Atletico Madrid, Martinez was not included in the Villa side for the home defeat by Crystal Palace – a display just as bad as the Brighton one.

Martinez is still at Villa today, still trying to get out, though he knuckled down last season and helped the club win the Europa League. So it would be foolish to write off Watkins’ Villa career just yet.

The Saudi Pro League’s top clubs can also be ruthless. If they decide a target is no longer worth pursuing, they will move on. Right now, that is the nightmare scenario for Watkins.

Yet the best outcome for all parties is probably to agree a deal. Watkins would have a huge job winning over Villa fans again. If he moves, he will have his new chapter and Villa will be able to pursue his replacement.

If Watkins stays Villa will give him a new deal, but that risks a loveless marriage. Despite the late goal rush, there were signs last season that Watkins was in decline. Do player or club really want to be tied to one another for the next two or three seasons?

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal. In midfield, they hope Leon Goretzka will arrive while there have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez, even though he is injured.

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal

There have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez (right), even though he is injured. Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they host Arsenal on Monday

Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they take on Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday.

With both Abraham and Madjo still struggling, one of Villa’s best-ever forwards risks being booed by some of his own fans in their first home game of the season, against the team he supported.

If nothing else, that prospect should focus a few minds.

Sports.title: Chelsea write to fans to urge them to stop singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' after chant was aired against at Fulham
Sports.content:
Chelsea write to fans to urge them to stop singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' after chant was aired against at Fulham

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea are to write to fans – and warn them of potential bans – after a section of the club’s support launched into a sectarian chant at their 3-2 win at Fulham.

During the west London derby a chorus of the ‘Flute for 50 pence song’ was clearly audible from the away section at Craven Cottage.

The song includes the line ‘F*** the Pope and the IRA’ and its airing would appear to reflect the long-standing relationship between elements of the club’s support and that of Glasgow Rangers.

Chelsea officials are aware of the chant, which is thought to have seen a resurgence in recent times, and have decided to act.

Daily Mail Sport understands they will trace those who bought tickets for the fixture, and email them to ask them to avoid any repeat. It is likely to be made clear that anyone found doing so will face a ban from attending matches.

The Football Association is thought to be aware of the situation.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham's new £85m signing wants to be called Savio not Savinho... as boss Roberto De Zerbi tells new man the area he must improve
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi hailed Savinho among the world's best one-on-one dribblers and told Tottenham's new signing it was now time to add goals to his game.

Spurs will pay Manchester City up to £85million for the Brazil international who wants to be known from this point forward as Savio.

The 22-year-old was named by his father in tribute to Savio, a Brazil winger who played for Flamengo and Real Madrid at the turn of the century.

He became known as Savinho, informally Little Savio, a common derivative in Latin America football, during a meteoric rise through Brazil's youth ranks.

The precise name on his No.17 shirt is the least of De Zerbi's problems after losing 3-0 at Brentford on Saturday.

De Zerbi is simply delighted to sign a player he tried to sign from Troyes when he was in charge at Brighton and who Spurs have been actively chasing for more than a year.

'We need players capable to win one-on-ones, to create something, create chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'In terms of the one-on-one he's one of the best. He can play right or left side. He's a big player for us, a big signing.'

Savio is still young, but his progress has stalled at City where he has scored two Premier League goals in two years since signing from City Group sister club Troyes after scoring 11 goals in 41 games during a season on loan at Girona in Spain.

Roberto De Zerbi has hailed new £85million signing Savinho after his arrival from Man City

The Brazilian wants to be known as 'Savio' after completing his move to the North Londoners

'To be complete he has to score,' said De Zerbi. 'If you analyse the best wingers in the world, many of them score 10-15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe he has to change habits because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-vs-one dribbling and also to score.

'Because we have to increase the number of chances to score and the number of goals. You become a top team scoring more goals.'

As for the delay in signing Savio, De Zerbi added: 'I am not patient. We started the negotiations for Savio three days or a week after the Everton game [in May] and for many reasons he arrived in the last week of August.

'If you want the highest quality level of players, it's right to wait. We always have a Plan B or Plan C, but players are not like smartphones. They're different so they come with different personalities, experiences, characteristics, potential.'

Spurs are also close to signing City's Omar Marmoush, initially on loan with an obligation to buy next year for £50m and working on a deal for Cody Gakpo from Liverpool ahead of the transfer deadline on Monday.

Spurs boss De Zerbi has told the Brazilian he needs to improve his goalscoring numbers

Signing players from successful clubs is integral to De Zerbi's bid to impose a winning mentality on his team, and he will insist they approach Tuesday's Carabao Cup second round tie at home against Charlton of the Championship like a Premier League fixture.

'We have to play well and get used to winning matches and matches,' said De Zerbi. 'Not one match, but one, two, three and four matches. We have to change the mood and we can. The environment has to change the players have to change this mentality.'

Savio is eligible to play against Charlton. Dominic Solanke is set to start with new captain Micky van de Ven and new vice-captain Pedro Porro back on the bench. James Maddison will not be involved after picking up a minor shoulder injury against Brentford.

Sports.title: Value Scope Extra: Steve Jones's horses to follow from the last seven days
Sports.content:
We've all been there. You start a new job, all keen to impress, but an attractive co-worker keeps providing an unwelcome distraction. As much as you try, it’s just impossible to keep your mind on the job.

So, spare a thought for GOD GIVEN TALENT. He made his handicap debut in a hot nursery at York’s Ebor Festival last Wednesday. It was his first start since joining William Haggas from former trainer James Ferguson, hopes were high as he took his place in the starting stalls but, unfortunately, his eye was drawn to a filly in the next berth.

From then his racing game face was replaced by a doe-eyed expression of love and his concentration went out of the Knavesmire window.

Jockey banned from riding for six months after police called to changing room punch-up READ MORE :

He found himself last of the 18 runners in the early stages and he’d only passed one with two of the six furlongs left to cover. Despite finding all sorts of traffic problems, he stormed home into fourth and he is clearly a well-handicapped horse with Group-race potential.

‌



Keep your eyes peeled for him in the near future, but he is likely to really come into his own next season.

COMMAND THE STARS is another horse to follow after from the Ebor Festival. He had been disappointing this year, considering he was a progressive two-year-old last season.

View 3 Images Command The Stars (red and blue, right) is a horse to follow (Image: Getty Images)

His trainer, George Scott, had tried a hood and longer distances, all to no avail. When he lined up in the Sky Bet Mile it was surely more in hope than expectation but he ran really well, despite stumbling and almost coming down early on. He recovered travelling well in midfield behind all-the-way winner Blue Courvoisier, without having a clear passage.

‌



A strongly-run big-field handicap is the key and he could easily develop into a Cambridgeshire contender. He is a general 66-1 shot for the Newmarket prize.

View 3 Images Joseph O'Brien: trainer of Monogram (Image: PA)

The top Classic prospect to run last week probably didn’t go anywhere near York. There was plenty of interest around MONOGRAM ahead of his debut at the Curragh and not just because he was a first Juddmonte-owned runner for Joseph O’Brien.

The two-year-old son of Kingman was backed into odds-on and, although he only got up close home, he clearly has top-class potential.

‌



Quotes of 20-1 for next year’s 2,000 Guineas were understandable and expect to see him in some of the top juvenile races in the latter months of the season.

Sports.title: Gary Neville has predicted Man Utd top-four finish nine years in a row with mixed results
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has predicted Man Utd top-four finish nine years in a row with mixed results

Gary Neville has consistently predicted Manchester United to finish high in the Premier League table over the years

View 3 Images Gary Neville looks to be a man of tradition when it comes to his former club (Image: Morgan Harlow/R&A/R&A via Getty Images)

Gary Neville has continued the trend of predicting Manchester United to finish in the top four of the Premier League table. Since the 2018/19 season, the ex-defender has backed his former club to secure Champions League football every year.

‌



Initially, Neville had put United third this year but switched his decision to fourth after their dismal 2-0 loss against Hull City. Speaking on Sky Sports, the 51-year-old said: "Look, do you want me to be honest? Yes. I can't separate United and Liverpool in fourth place."

‌



Jamie Carragher wasn't pleased with this and replied: "I've heard you've changed it four times over the weekend. So after United played, he changed it to Liverpool. Liverpool played and he changed it to United."

‌



Neville then said: "A couple of weeks ago, I had United in third. Look, at the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, really, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates READ MORE :

Carrick snaps at reporter over 'ridiculous' question after Man Utd defeat READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football have examined Neville's predictions over the last nine campaigns and how close he was.

2018/19 - Wrong

In the 18/19 season, Neville had United in third. That year, Jose Mourinho was sacked in December and replaced by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who guided them to sixth place.

‌



2019/20 - Right

Solskjaer continued his run the following year with Neville believing United would go two places better and finish fourth. The ex-United star led the club to third and Champions League football.

2020/21 - Right

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher would often make predictions alongside Neville (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



In the 2020/21 campaign, Solskjaer was sacked three months in and was replaced by Ralf Rangnick as interim boss. They finished second - the same prediction Neville made at the start of the year.

2021/22 - Wrong

Erik ten Hag took over ahead of the 2021/22 campaign and Neville said he would keep them in the top three. He stated that United "have got to prove themselves."

Ten Hag began his reign with a sixth-place finish in the Premier League. The following year, United won the Carabao Cup against Newcastle and finished runner-up in the FA Cup to Pep Guardiola's Manchester City.

‌



2022/23 - Right

Neville put the Red Devils in the top four that year, stating: "I'm gonna put them as my fourth team," to which Carragher replied: "Every year this happens!"

United went one better and finished third in the 2022/23 campaign, winning silverware for the first time since 2017.

2023/24 - Wrong

The former club captain predicted Ten Hag's side to repeat this feat once more for the 2023/24 campaign, saying: "I think Arsenal can beat them [City] this year. Arsenal, City, Man United, Liverpool, Chelsea, [Aston] Villa."

‌



Ten Hag won another trophy, this time the FA Cup, but dropped down to an eighth-place finish in the league.

View 3 Images Gary Neville has top-four on his mind for Carrick (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

2024/25 - Wrong

By October, the Dutchman was sacked and Ruben Amorim was appointed to lead the charge.

‌



Neville had the Red Devils finishing third in the league before Ten Hag's dismissal and Amorim's arrival. The Portuguese manager would lead United to their worst-ever Premier League placement, finishing 15th and losing the Europa League final to Tottenham.

2025/26 - Right

Despite this nightmare start for Amorim, Neville was optimistic that United would improve significantly in the 2025/26 season. He had them fourth for last year and confirmed this when Sky Sports presenter David Jones asked: "Thirteen per cent of Manchester United fans think they will finish in the top four. 13 per cent... Have we got one per cent here?"

Neville replied: "Course we have. I can't disappoint you. I've got to come back here in 10 months and try to defend this. So, David, we've worked out before that I've done this now for eight years and I've always had Manchester United in the top four, every year."

Amorim departed in January after another poor start and Carrick returned to lead United to a third-placed finish.

Sports.title: Race meeting abandoned after Dylan Browne McMonagle taken to hospital following fall
Sports.content:
Race meeting abandoned after Dylan Browne McMonagle taken to hospital following fall

Champion jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle was unseated when riding the Joseph O'Brien-trained Mosel in the opening race at Bellewstown on Tuesday and was taken to hospital following the fall.

View 2 Images Dylan Browne McMonagle: taken to hospital after fall (Image: PA)

Racing at Bellewstown on Tuesday was abandoned after champion jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle suffered an injury following a fall in the opening race.

‌



McMonagle was aboard the Joseph O'Brien-trained Mosel when the filly lost her footing and unseated the Donegal rider at the furlong pole. The 23-year-old remained conscious and was treated on the track by the racecourse medical team for several minutes, causing a delay to the 4.55 race.

‌



He was subsequently taken by ambulance to Drogheda Hospital, with an IHRB update confirming: "Dylan Browne McMonagle is conscious and being transferred to hospital in Drogheda.

‌



Nicky Henderson announces decision on Constitution Hill Windsor appearance READ MORE :

Arc-winning trainer announces stable closure with business set to go into liquidation READ MORE :

"There will be a delay of approximately 10 minutes to the start of Race 2 at @BellewstownRace as parts of the track are being sanded."

The race eventually got under way at 5.25pm — a full 30 minutes behind schedule — and further incidents followed, with two additional horses slipping on the sodden surface and throwing their riders.

An inspection of the track took place with jockeys and trainers present to examine an area on the bend after which the rest of the meeting was called off.

‌



The IHRB said: "The Raceday Stewards met with a delegation of riders, the IHRB Clerk of the Course, representatives of the Irish Racehorse Trainers Association and the Racecourse Manager to review an incident on the bend.

"Having reviewed the footage and considered the observations, as well as the remedial work carried out following Race 1, the Raceday Stewards, in the interest of safety for both horse and rider, made the decision to abandon the remainder of the card under the provisions of Rule 10."

View 2 Images Dylan Browne McMonagle: Ireland's Flat champion (Image: PA)

Article continues below

The much-loved County Meath venue is marking its 300th anniversary this week, but the troubling events across the opening two races will undoubtedly have cast a shadow over the celebrations.

McMonagle's fall comes hot on the heels of several other jockeys sustaining injuries at Killarney last week. Gary Noonan was airlifted to hospital at the Kerry track on Friday with serious injuries and remains in hospital with multiple broken ribs, punctures to both lungs and a broken shoulder blade.

Amateur rider Joey Dunne was left hospitalised with a fractured jaw, while conditional jockey Paddy O'Brien suffered fractures to both his pelvis and a vertebra in his back.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham's £85m swoop for Savio just doesn't add up - except for Man City
Sports.content:
Why Tottenham's £85m swoop for Savio just doesn't add up - except for Man City

Rafi Moersen was the brains behind City's decision to sign Brazilian flop Savio - and has now done it again on behalf of Spurs - for £50m more in a deal which is difficult to fathom

View 2 Images Savinho has cost Tottenham a staggering £85m (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Senior figures at Manchester City are said to be thrilled with the sale of Savio to Tottenham in a deal which could reach £85m.

‌



And so they should be. Because somehow, City have managed to make more than £50m profit on a footballer who contributed little or nothing to the team's success in the short time he spent at the Etihad.

‌



It took Pep Guardiola less than half a season to realise he'd made a mistake in signing the Brazilian winger from Troyes in 2024. In two seasons in Manchester, Savio made just 28 league appearances. These included a grand total of seven last season. But it was his lack of commitment as much as his lack of impression and goals, which made the £30.8m fee look extortionate.

‌



Let's just say Guardiola and his coaching staff had little time for Savio's work rate and reluctance to get physical when he needed to. But there is a man working at the highest level of football who must see something in Savinho no-one else can: Carlos Raphael Moersen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Moersen, who is known as 'Rafi" to his friends and colleagues, oversaw Savio's transfer to City when he was the City Football Group executive.

‌



He spent almost a decade working across CFG clubs and, and was responsible for overseeing football transactions within the organisation. In December of 2025 Moersen was lured to Tottenham, as the club's new director of football operations. Moersen arrived in north London with big ideas.

And it just so happens one of them was for Spurs to sign Savio. Which they have now done. Signing someone who looks out of his depth in the Premier League once, is clumsy. But doing the same thing twice is downright foolish. Undeterred, Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi is under the impression he's landed himself a game-changing star.

View 2 Images Savinho failed to make an impact at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity," he said.

Spurs' fascination with Savio is as remarkable as it is hard to fathom. Because, and with respect to De Zerbi, if Guardiola didn't rate him, then why would an Italian whose greatest managerial achievement to date is winning the Ukrainian Super Cup?

Spurs supporters should be bracing themselves. To witness a footballer who flatters to deceive - thus personifying what his new club have been all about in recent times.

Sports.title: Man Utd announce Carlos Baleba transfer in £70m deal as next signing becomes clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce Carlos Baleba transfer in £70m deal as next signing becomes clear

Carlos Baleba has signed a five-year contract with Manchester United, who've finally completed their midfield rebuild with just one week to go before the summer transfer window slams shut

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba has officially joined Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have announced the signing of Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70million. Baleba, 22, has put pen to paper on a five-year contract at Old Trafford, with the option of the further 12 months, and leaves Brighton after three impressive seasons.

‌



United will pay an initial £65m plus a potential £5m in add-ons. Brighton have also negotiated a sell-on clause for the midfielder they bought from French side Lille in 2023.

‌



Baleba becomes the Red Devils' third midfield signing of the summer, joining Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m). United will now focus on other areas during the final week of the transfer window, with left-back a priority.

‌



Contact has been made for Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, who was left out of their squad to face Elche on Sunday. A forward is also on United's shopping list, but that may depend on the future of Joshua Zirkzee.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Having completed his medical over the weekend, Baleba said: "It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

‌



United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, added: "Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

"We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

"Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions."

‌



Who should Manchester United sign next? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester United wanted to sign Carlos Baleba a year ago (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Baleba isn't expected to make his debut until next month, with the Cameroon international nursing an ankle ligament injury which ruled him out of Brighton's first two games. United host Ipswich this Sunday looking for their first point of the season, as Michael Carrick's side suffered an abject 2-0 defeat away to Hull in their opening Premier League game.

‌



Their need for a player like Baleba was no more evident than against Hull, as they sorely lacked a midfielder capable of covering ground and winning back possession. United did the groundwork on the 22-year-old last summer when Brighton quoted United £100m for his services.

But the club's patience has paid off, signing him for a considerably lower fee this time around. His arrival takes United's spending to £155m, with their other newcomer, goalkeeper Karl Darlow, joining on a free after his contract with Leeds expired.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
