Sports.title: What makes Norris say “I don't have a car to fight for the championship”?
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 championship finds itself at a curious intersection where nobody is willing to entertain the idea that they have the best car.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after finishing second to Lando Norris in the Dutch Grand Prix that Mercedes no longer has the best car – indeed, that it may only be the third best.

But Norris, now fourth in the standings with 159 points to Antonelli’s 242, was determined to play down talk of him staging a comeback in the final half of the season, despite winning two consecutive grands prix. "I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship," he said after his Dutch GP victory.

Many readers would be tempted to cite the so-called Mandy Rice-Davies principle – "Well they would say that, wouldn’t they?"

What’s clear, though, is that under the latest technical regulations there is still a difference in relative strengths between cars which complicates the competitive picture. In broad-brush terms the McLaren MCL40 thrives in fast corners, Ferrari’s SF-26 is strong in terms of carrying good speed into slow corners, while the Mercedes W17 is somewhere between the two. That makes the competitive balance heavily dependent on circuit layout.

Norris’s contention is that his car is insufficiently rounded to be dominant across the remaining rounds in the way last year’s McLaren was the car to beat at most tracks.

Norris played down the significance of his Dutch GP victory Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We have a strong car in certain areas," he said. "It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere. We're very, very strong in high speed. The place we've improved the car the most is high-speed performance.

"No one matches us in high speed. And that's a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn 7, Turn 8 was crazy.

"But their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore I don't have the confidence to say, yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. I know I've just won two races in a row and two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship.

"And I know that's quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed from me. And I know the level that I am now and what I can perform at. And I know just what I need from the car – and what tracks we have coming up where we're going to certainly struggle more."

The issue is more complex than simply saying a particular car is fast around a certain type of corner. This year’s cars are shorter, narrower and slightly lighter – and the chassis characteristics are more interconnected with power unit performance than ever before, given the influence of corner-entry speeds on energy harvesting.

McLaren's decision to run a short wheelbase, helping it save weight at the start of the season, has baked in certain shortcomings in terms of how much aerodynamic load the team can squeeze from the floor.

Performance is often hugely variable between tyre compounds. In Saturday’s sprint race, running mediums, Norris struggled with rear degradation and was overtaken by Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in the closing stages. In the grand prix he took the restart on used softs, was passed by Antonelli at the start, and didn’t really get into the race until the hard-compound tyres went on.

Norris was able to pressure championship leader Antonelli later in the Zandvoort race Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

"We put on the hard tyres," he said. "We were a bit more aggressive with how we wanted to approach the stint. And we turned things around. I had that feeling in the car that I wanted. I went from just not feeling like I was going to win a race to at least we can force him [Antonelli] to make mistakes.

"When I get what I need from a car, when I have the front I want, when I get the confidence with the rear on entries – just when I get what I need to be able to know and predict every single corner, I'm going to win a race."

Norris has a driving style slightly more aligned to Max Verstappen than the likes of George Russell or even his own team-mate, Oscar Piastri. Rather than separating the throttle off/brake on and turning phases, he likes to blend the throttle and brakes and take a shallower approach angle. Essentially he is feeling for the point in the overlap where the front tyres begin to exert more lateral grip, which helps rotate the car and carry more speed into the corner, towards the apex.

This requires the car not only to have a 'strong' front end, but also to communicate what the front tyres are doing, which represents a tough engineering challenge. Modern F1 cars require a consistent ride height for the aerodynamics to function optimally, so the suspension geometry is designed to minimise dive and squat. A side of this is that it saps driver 'feel'.

Some can live with that, some can’t, which is why McLaren designed an alternate front suspension geometry with a revised kingpin angle for Norris when he was floundering at the beginning of last season. Once he has that feel he can be very adaptable in terms of his lines and the degree of overlap between throttle and brake, which is why he thrives in low-grip conditions.

But although he has a huge amount of adaptability within this range, he still needs that strong front end, good transmission of feel, and confidence that the rear axle will rotate predictably on cue.

"It's clear where our weaknesses are," Norris concluded. "Therefore we need to attack those things. And until we do that, it's still going to be a very tough end of the season."

Sports.title: FIA explains safety car formation lap after F1 driver criticism at Dutch GP
Sports.content:
The opening stages of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort descended into chaos after rain had started to fall during the grid procedure.

Max Verstappen crashed heavily on the exit of the final corner on the opening lap of the race. The Red Bull driver admitted that it was entirely his own mistake. The Dutchman thought he could get back on the throttle, but that part of the track was clearly still too wet.

Behind Verstappen, Gabriel Bortoleto also came close to crashing, although he miraculously managed to keep his Audi out of the wall, while it was even more remarkable that team-mate Nico Hulkenberg managed to avoid him.

The German immediately said over the radio that he feared he was going to T-bone Bortoleto.

"It was just that corner, if I'm very honest with you. It was full wets, that place. I think that's why Max lost it and it was the same for me," Bortoleto said in the media pen post-race.

"I was on the downside of the banking. I did a little reaction move to the left, I think, when I saw big smoke coming up ahead. And when I did that, I just went as well."

According to Gasly, F1 drivers would have been able to get their tyres up to temperature more effectively if the formation lap had been completed without the safety car Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Would a normal formation lap have been better?

According to the drivers, the rest of the track had already dried by that point, meaning it was simply a matter of surviving the final two corners. Starting on slicks therefore made sense, as did the FIA’s decision to opt for a standing start.

That said, several drivers were critical of how the start procedure was carried out at Zandvoort.

"If we would go the way we did with one lap behind the safety car and a standing start, then I would have preferred to just do a normal out-lap, so we would have pushed a bit faster,” Pierre Gasly said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I thought the point was to go at least once through the last corner and the banking with the safety car before doing the normal race start. And yeah, it was damp."

According to the Alpine driver, the FIA would have been better off choosing between two conventional options: a rolling start behind the safety car or a standing start with a normal formation lap.

"I'm sure we'll review at the next race what the drivers' feedback was," Gasly continued. "But I think it was either no safety car and only one formation lap or with the safety car at least giving us one extra lap."

Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson shared that view and added that he already knew before the start that the procedure would lead to chaos.

Lawson emphasises that he deliberately left more margin than his team-mate Verstappen in the final corner Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

"I don't know why we had the safety car. To do a standing start and also do a lap behind the safety car makes no sense," Lawson said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I'm not sure what the reasoning of that was, but I feel like we could all see that coming. We were all probably saying the same thing before when we got the news, but we didn't have control over that."

FIA explains reasoning behind safety car formation lap

When asked by Motorsport.com, the FIA clarified that it acted on the information available at the time.

The race director first sent the medical car out for a reconnaissance lap, something an FIA spokesperson said does not normally happen.

The feedback from the medical car was that there was still standing water at Turns 2 and 3, with Turn 3 – the Hugenholtz corner – also being the first banked corner on the circuit. Based on that information, the FIA considered it safer to complete the formation lap behind the safety car.

The intention at that point was to have a standing start, but by completing the formation lap behind the safety car, race control kept both options open. If the standing water had been deemed too dangerous, it could still have opted for a rolling start.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz, however, felt the latter would not have been a solution and would not have prevented the chaos in the final corner.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I think, given it was towards the end of the lap, a non-standing start, a rolling start, would have ended up in the same result, because by that time we were all one by one," Sainz said. "So I don't think it would have changed much. It's an unfortunate situation with a lot of water in only one corner."

It therefore came down to the drivers’ own judgement, with Lawson stressing that he deliberately left more margin – considerably more than Verstappen, who was running ahead of him.

"It was just impossible. The whole first half of the lap was dry and then the last few corners were completely soaked. So, it was really easy to do that [what Max has done] when you have this much power on a slick tyre," he said.

"I really lifted out of it because honestly I had no confidence in how much grip we were going to have there and I think Max was probably trying to get closer and make an overtake, and just lost it."

Verstappen himself, however, did not want to blame any external factors and stressed that he had simply made a mistake.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Expects Fury-Joshua Fight in America
Sports.content:
“I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Alalshikh, he will announce that fairly soon. I know there’s been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out. In the meantime, Tyson has flown off to the States. He’s in Miami, and he’s preparing for the fight,” said Warren to Sky Sports News.

Fury recently placed the fight in “serious doubt” and accused Joshua of wanting more money after plans moved away from a British stadium. Eddie Hearn has argued that Joshua signed for a UK event and that staging it in America would reduce his earnings after taxes while adding obligations to the contract.

That account undercuts the suggestion that Joshua alone wants to keep the event in Britain. Warren said Fury also prefers Wembley, but the broadcaster and financial backers have chosen America.

“They could refuse to fight. We don’t get the fight we want to see,” Warren said. “I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I’m wrong, but I think it will go on in America.”

Much depends on how determined Joshua and Hearn are to increase his purse or force a return to the original terms. Hearn has openly rejected the venue change without amendments to Joshua’s contract, added payment and other demands from Alalshikh’s side.

Those public complaints may also have irritated Alalshikh, Sela and TKO Boxing. Joshua has lost the ability to negotiate the way he did during his prime. He has no world title, lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk and was knocked out by Daniel Dubois.

His last fight further weakened his position. Kristian Prenga was brought in for a showcase tune-up, but the second-tier heavyweight dropped Joshua twice in the opening round. Joshua was saved by the bell before returning to stop Prenga in the second.

Hearn can demand more money for moving the event, but the organizers have far less reason to agree to it than they would have had six years ago. The Prenga scare gave them another reason not to treat Joshua like one of the best heavyweights in the division.

This matchup is roughly six years past the point when it carried its greatest sporting value. Fury and Joshua once held every major heavyweight title between them, but repeated negotiations never brought them into the same ring. Usyk eventually beat both men and took away the argument over which one was the best heavyweight of their generation.

Fury has declined as well. He lost twice to Usyk before retiring and returning when another enormous payday became available. Training in Miami does not change what has happened to him or Joshua.

No longer a contest to determine Britain’s best heavyweight or the leading fighter in the division, it is now a nostalgia event for supporters who followed both men during their primes. The fight still makes money because of who Fury and Joshua used to be, not because of what either man has left.

Joshua may have the contractual right to reject America, but using it risks losing a payday that may never return. Hearn can continue pressing for revised terms, although his case weakens if the financial backers decide the price is too high for a fight between two heavyweights who are shot to pieces.

Eddie Hearn: Nobody Can Stop Fury-Joshua Fight

Eddie Hearn insists Anthony Joshua’s fight with Tyson Fury remains legally binding and can only collapse if Sela breaches the signed agreement.

Fury claimed Friday that the fight no longer looked likely, blaming Joshua and Hearn for seeking more money. Hearn has now rejected that account, maintaining that both fighters are signed and Joshua’s side is only waiting for Sela to provide a date.

“The update is quite simple. We’ve signed the contract. We’re waiting for a date. You saw Tyson Fury on the elliptical trainer, shouting and screaming. There’s nothing to shout about. The fight’s done, the fight’s signed,” Hearn told DAZN Boxing. “No one can pull out of the fight. You can’t just pull out of a contract. So, we’re waiting on the date.”

The dispute remains tied to the location. Joshua’s agreement calls for the fight to take place in the UK, while Sela, Netflix and the other parties involved favor New York. Hearn has submitted separate terms that would allow Joshua to accept Madison Square Garden, but he made clear that his preference remains a British stadium.

If Sela rejects those changes, Hearn expects the company to follow the existing contract and deliver the event in the UK.

“If they deliver on the contract, which they have to legally, the fight’s happening in the UK, and we’ll be very, very happy,” Hearn said. “The only way it can stop from happening is if they actually breach the contract.”

That line leaves Sela with two direct options: honor the UK agreement or meet Joshua’s terms for America. Sela can still abandon the event in practice, but doing so may expose the company to a costly legal claim. The possible damages cannot be calculated without seeing the cancellation and breach provisions.

Hearn’s claim is legally forceful but practically overstated. Sela cannot withdraw without risking financial penalties, but it can still refuse to finance the event. A contract creates legal consequences for breaking an agreement; it does not guarantee that a boxing match reaches the ring.

The greater issue may come after the lawyers finish. Joshua has received some of his largest purses through Turki Alalshikh and Sela. Hearn can use the UK clause to secure better terms for New York, but pushing too far risks damaging the relationship that makes paydays of this size possible. Few other backers can offer Joshua comparable money at this stage of his career.

Sports.title: How Boxing Turned Sonny Liston Into Its Monster
Sports.content:
There were legitimate reasons to scrutinize him. Liston’s history included prison time for armed robbery, further arrests and ties to men with organized crime interests in boxing. Frankie Carbo and Frank “Blinky” Palermo held financial interests in his career. Reporters were justified in questioning those relationships.

The coverage frequently went beyond examining his history. It allowed that history to obscure every other part of him. Boxing offered Liston no rehabilitation story, even though prison was where he learned to box and found the skill that gave him a legal profession. His past was not presented as something he had survived. It became proof that he remained permanently dangerous.

Race also influenced how America saw him. Patterson was considered respectable, articulate and safe for the heavyweight title. Liston became the large, scowling Black man coming to take it away. His size, stare, and criminal record were packaged together until the fighter disappeared behind the character.

Liston did little to soften that image because he never looked comfortable performing for the press. He rarely smiled, gave short answers, and looked ill at ease during interviews. Reporters often interpreted his discomfort as hostility. He lacked the education, confidence and media training to present another version of himself.

Other Black heavyweight champions had qualities that helped reassure or captivate the public. Joe Louis projected quiet dignity. Patterson displayed sensitivity and vulnerability. Muhammad Ali later controlled every room through humor, intelligence, and language. Liston possessed none of those qualities. His silence allowed promoters and reporters to define him.

Destroying Patterson strengthened the monster boxing had created. Liston knocked him out in 2:06 at Comiskey Park, then required only four additional seconds to repeat the result in their July 1963 rematch. Those victories should have confirmed his place as an exceptional heavyweight. Instead, they made him look cruel.

The performances were also reduced to physical intimidation. Liston possessed enormous strength and punching power, but he was not an unskilled bully. His long jab controlled distance, his body punches weakened opponents, and his ability to cut off the ring prevented smaller heavyweights from escaping. Cleveland Williams and Zora Folley were beaten by a technically developed fighter, not merely a frightening man with heavy hands.

Cassius Clay understood Liston’s public identity and used it against him. He mocked Liston’s appearance, age and intelligence before taking the championship in February 1964. When Liston remained on his stool after the sixth round, the supposedly indestructible champion was recast as a coward. The disputed first-round finish in their 1965 rematch added another permanent stain.

Questions about those fights have followed Liston for decades, but they now overshadow almost everything he accomplished. His mob associations, two losses to Ali and mysterious death dominate his story. His jab, strength and destruction of the leading heavyweights of his era receive far less attention.

Liston contributed to his reputation through his criminal activity and the people surrounding his career. Those facts ultimately swallowed every other part of him. Boxing built a monster, profited from the fear, and discarded the man once Ali supplied the sport with a more charismatic champion.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic PREVIEW
Sports.content:
The heavyweight division has been in total disarray ever since Oleksandr Usyk made the unprecedented move of dropping his remaining alphabet belts. That maneuver threw the entire championship landscape into chaos, opening the door for this massive showdown. If Itauma wins, at just 21 years and 8 months old, he officially becomes the second youngest heavyweight in history to win a major world title, surpassing Floyd Patterson and trailing only Iron Mike Tyson. A victory for Hrgovic, meanwhile, would represent the ultimate career redemption.

The central storyline heading into this one is a familiar one. Itauma is young, fast, and devastatingly explosive. His knockout power is unquestioned. But the two biggest questions surrounding the young prodigy continue to remain completely unanswered: his chin, and his stamina when the going gets tough. Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin were both supposed to provide those answers, but Itauma blasted Whyte out in one round and became the first man to ever stop Franklin.

Hrgovic brings legitimate world-class toughness and a proven granite chin, having absorbed terrifying artillery against Big Bang Zhang, Daniel Dubois, and Joe Joyce. The problem for Hrgovic, however, is that he remains mechanical, telegraphs his big right hand, and cuts easily around the eyes once the leather starts flying. Against a razor-sharp counterpuncher with blistering hand speed like Itauma, that is an absolute nightmare matchup.

Who will win the upcoming fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner will contemplate the question while also providing a quick preview of the showdown between Itauma and Hrgovic. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: Alycia Baumgardner Challenges Elif Nur Turhan November 8
Sports.content:
Baumgardner controlled the championship picture at 130 pounds before choosing to chase another belt five pounds north. She receives no settling-in fight at lightweight.

Turhan can punch.

The Turkish champion seized the IBF belt by stopping Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira in the fifth round last December. She has since beaten Taylah Gentzen and Gabriella Tellez and enters November making her third title defense.

That finishing power gives Baumgardner a different problem to solve. She owns the quicker feet and sharp counters, but Turhan can close distance, set her base and punish mistakes with combinations once she forces her opponent into exchanges.

Baumgardner believes her championship experience will travel with her.

“When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different,” Baumgardner said. “I know what it takes to become undisputed. I’ve done it before, and I’ll do it again.”

Turhan expects Baumgardner to attack rather than simply box for points.

“As two boxers sharing a ‘win at all costs’ mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight, and only one winner.”

Three additional championship fights give the Arlington card depth.

WBC featherweight champion Tiara Brown defends against former undisputed champion Ellie Scotney, who climbs to 126 pounds chasing a championship in a second division. Brown brings strength and pressure, while Scotney will try to dictate the distance with her feet and combinations.

Skye Nicolson defends her WBC super bantamweight championship against three-time, two-division champion Miyo Yoshida in her MVP debut. Nicolson will look to establish her southpaw jab and control the ring positioning after injury forced their previous date to be scrapped.

Ramla Ali battles Mikiah Kreps for unified super bantamweight championships, completing the four-title-fight card.

Baumgardner’s move supplies the main tactical question. She cannot afford to stand at Turhan’s preferred distance and trade simply to prove she belongs at lightweight. Baumgardner needs to start with the jab, use her footwork and make Turhan pay with counters before the champion can set her feet.

If Turhan consistently gets inside and starts working the body, Baumgardner will find out quickly how much harder five additional pounds can punch.

Sports.title: Matchroom Presses WBA To Force Teofimo Lopez vs. Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
“When I met Gilberto Mendoza in Egypt, I shook his hand and he gave me his word if I beat Giyasov, someone who was avoided and waited for his shot for two years, I will get my shot within 180 days regardless who has the belt. So I believe the WBA will do the correct thing,” Catterall posted.

That account removes much of the uncertainty about what the WBA intended. Its published resolution named Rolando Romero, but its president allegedly told Catterall that the commitment followed the title. Lopez still has a technical argument based on the written wording, yet the WBA would have to break Mendoza’s personal promise to let him move on.

The dispute began after Lopez openly denied that Catterall was his mandatory during Monday’s Inside the Ring show. Lopez plans to pursue the three additional titles he needs to become the undisputed welterweight champion, beginning with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn on September 12.

That pursuit leaves no place for Catterall, but the secondary WBA champion has rejected the easiest negotiated solution.

“There’s not $1 that can persuade me to step aside to allow a unification bout to happen. I’m here to fight,” Catterall said.

His refusal means Matchroom cannot be paid to wait while Lopez pursues the Garcia vs. Benn winner. The WBA must enforce the consolidation fight, permit a unification first, or allow its two welterweight champions to remain separated.

The 180-day period expires on November 19, based on Catterall’s May 23 victory over Shakhram Giyasov. That leaves less than three months to settle the dispute. The cut Lopez suffered over his right eyebrow against Rolando Romero places more strain on the schedule, although there has been no indication that it will keep him out for an extended period.

Teofimo may believe the WBA will permit a unification to take priority over its internal consolidation fight. Sanctioning bodies regularly move mandatory obligations aside when champions pursue another belt, giving his team a stronger argument than the wording omission alone.

Catterall brings tactical risk with little financial reward. His awkward southpaw style and sharp counterpunching deny opponents clean offensive opportunities. Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn and Devin Haney generate massive paydays. Catterall brings no comparable commercial appeal, only a genuine threat to expose Lopez inside the ring.

WBA Loophole Gives Teofimo Lopez Easy Out On Jack Catterall

A review of the WBA’s published rulings supports part of Teofimo Lopez’s argument. No public order currently names Jack Catterall as the mandatory challenger for Lopez’s newly acquired Super welterweight title.

The May 21 ruling required Rolando Romero to face the Catterall-Shakhram Giyasov winner within 180 days. Its language named Romero specifically. It did not say the obligation would transfer to Romero’s successor if the title changed hands.

That omission gives Lopez a technical basis for denying that Catterall has been formally assigned to him. The WBA would need to issue another ruling, clarify that the original order followed the championship, or designate Catterall as Lopez’s challenger.

Teofimo still goes too far by claiming Catterall was lied to. The WBA sanctioned the Giyasov bout and publicly stated that its winner would receive Romero within 180 days. Catterall’s expectation came directly from the organization, not from an invented promise by his team.

The real issue is poor wording from the WBA. It created two champions and ordered them to meet, yet attached the obligation to Romero by name rather than clearly attaching it to the Super title. Lopez is now using that opening to pursue the Garcia-Benn winner while Catterall waits for the WBA to explain what its own ruling means.

Teofimo Lopez Denies Jack Catterall Mandatory Status

Teofimo Lopez claims Jack Catterall is not his WBA mandatory and says the British contender was lied to about his right to challenge for the welterweight title.

During today’s Inside the Ring show, Catterall confronted the new WBA champion after Lopez discussed facing the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner and eventually meeting Devin Haney for the undisputed championship.

“He’s not. He’s not my mandatory,” Lopez said when Catterall was identified as next in line. “By the sanctioning rules, he’s not my mandatory, and I think they lied. I think they lied to him.”

“It’s in the contract,” Catterall answered.

Teofimo’s denial conflicts with the WBA’s own published ruling. When the organization elevated Rolando Romero to Super champion in May, it sanctioned Catterall’s bout with Shakhram Giyasov for the vacant secondary title and stated that Romero had to face the winner within 180 days.

Catterall defeated Giyasov and now holds that belt. Lopez may argue that the ruling named Romero rather than whoever defeated him, or that no separate order has been issued since Saturday. Neither explanation supports his claim that Catterall was lied to. The WBA publicly connected the two titles and imposed a deadline for bringing them together.

The exchange became entertaining because Lopez tried to rewrite the situation while Catterall was on the screen looking directly at him. Rather than explain the supposed sanctioning rule, Teofimo declared that the obligation did not exist and blamed unnamed people for misleading Catterall.

After making that denial, the new champion returned to the familiar claim that he will face anyone.

“I’m always willing to fight anybody and everybody,” Lopez said.

“I’m glad you won on the weekend because I know you don’t duck nobody,” Catterall replied. “It would have been more difficult to get Rolly into the ring. I’m happy for you, but we’ve got to get it on.”

Catterall played the interaction perfectly. He congratulated Lopez, reminded him that Romero would have been harder to bring into the ring and declined to turn the conversation into a shouting match. That left Teofimo arguing against a contract he had not seen while Catterall calmly insisted the terms were already written down.

There was also some clever pressure inside Catterall’s praise. Telling Lopez, “I know you don’t duck nobody,” gave the champion little room to reject the fight without contradicting the reputation Catterall had just assigned to him.

The WBA now needs to explain the status of its own ruling. It can grant Lopez permission to pursue a unification, arrange a step-aside payment or order the title consolidation. What it cannot credibly do is remain silent while its new champion claims the other titleholder was fooled.

Lopez is clearly trying to look past the mandatory to chase the massive paydays against the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner or a unification with Devin Haney. Catterall holds the regular belt after beating Shakhram Giyasov, which, in standard WBA procedure, makes him the direct mandatory to unify the titles.

Sports.title: Esteban De Jesús Shatters Roberto Durán’s Invincibility
Sports.content:
Durán had captured the WBA and Ring lightweight titles from Ken Buchanan five months earlier at the same arena. Two quick stoppages followed, and the 10-round meeting with De Jesús may have looked like another chance to stay active in New York.

His preparation was far from ideal. Durán had suffered an injured elbow and cuts to his lip in a car accident. Reports also described a young champion enjoying the rewards of his new position and treating the fight less seriously than De Jesús did.

Both boxers came in above the lightweight limit, with Durán at 137½ pounds and De Jesús at 138. That kept the championship belts out of reach, but the absence of titles did nothing to reduce the importance of what followed.

De Jesús was 22 years old and carried only one defeat on a record listed around 32-1 or 33-1. The former Puerto Rican lightweight champion possessed the timing, composure and left hook needed to punish Durán’s aggression.

Protecting his early advantage, De Jesús worked from range, used his jab and combinations, then caught Durán with the left hook when the champion tried to force his way inside.

The usual Durán pressure never fully arrived. He landed enough hard punches to remain dangerous, including a right hand during the eighth that forced De Jesús to clinch, but his attacks lacked their normal volume. Frustration showed in the fifth when referee Arthur Mercante warned him for hitting after the break and delivering a low blow. Both men continued punching after the bell in the eighth.

Ten rounds later, all three officials favored De Jesús before 9,144 spectators. Mercante gave him five rounds to Durán’s four, with one even. Harold Lederman scored six rounds for De Jesús and three for Durán, with one even, while Bill Recht gave De Jesús six rounds, Durán two, and scored two even. The $62,339 gate reflected the interest surrounding Durán’s New York return, but the night belonged to the Puerto Rican contender.

The defeat did not diminish Durán for long. It gave him a target.

Their second fight came in Panama in March 1974, this time with the WBA lightweight title at stake. De Jesús floored Durán again in the opening round, but the champion recovered and stopped him in the 11th.

The deciding meeting followed four years later in Las Vegas with the WBA and WBC championships on the line. Durán ended their rivalry by stopping De Jesús in the 12th round, completing his domination of the lightweight division before moving up in weight.

Competition eventually gave way to something deeper. In 1989, Durán visited De Jesús as his former opponent was dying from AIDS. He embraced and kissed him publicly during a period when fear and stigma surrounded the disease.

That 1972 upset remains one of the defining results of the decade. De Jesús did not catch an unknown prospect before his prime. He defeated the reigning lightweight champion, then forced one of boxing’s greatest fighters to spend the next six years proving that night would never happen again.

Sports.title: Joe Cordina Cannot Afford Another Wasted Year
Sports.content:
Stevenson withdrew after suffering a hand injury during training and underwent surgery. The cancellation cost Cordina a world title fight through no fault of his own, but Matchroom then needed nearly nine months to get him back into the ring.

Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz was a reasonable opponent for his lightweight return in July 2025. Coming back against a limited fighter made sense after the Cacace defeat, the Stevenson cancellation and more than a year outside the ring. The mistake was giving Cordina a second rebuilding fight five months later. Gabriel Flores Jr. carried a higher ranking and a recognizable name, but he presented little danger to a boxer with Cordina’s championship experience. One tune up should have been enough.

After defeating Flores by unanimous decision on December 13, Cordina became the WBO’s No. 1 lightweight contender. He then waited nearly seven months for a title fight against Abdullah Mason in Cleveland.

That date was lost when the United States embassy refused Cordina’s visa application. He had been charged following an alleged February incident in Cardiff and later pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault by beating. Cordina maintains that he acted in self defence, and his trial is scheduled for October 13.

The Stevenson cancellation was beyond Cordina’s control. The Mason situation cannot be treated in quite the same way. Whatever the trial ultimately decides, circumstances involving Cordina resulted in the visa refusal and removed him from the biggest fight available to him.

Matchroom should already have placed him on a UK card against a respectable lightweight, but Cordina also carries responsibility for demanding an active schedule. A 34 year old former champion cannot passively protect a No. 1 ranking while months of his career disappear. Even a 10 round bout would have kept him active and shown that he intended to remain a serious lightweight contender.

Since Cacace stopped him in May 2024, Cordina has fought only twice, and neither opponent showed how he would perform against a leading lightweight. His world championship experience means he does not require an extended rebuilding process.

Neither title fight took place, but the long periods surrounding them were avoidable. At 34, Cordina needs meaningful opposition, not another year spent waiting.

Sports.title: Lou DiBella Says Zuffa Will Seize U.S. Boxing Immediately
Sports.content:
The established companies had decades to reduce the number of titles, arrange the leading fights, and develop boxers into recognizable stars. Instead, promoters protected their champions as financial assets while the sanctioning bodies produced regular, interim, and super titles.

Becoming a champion consequently lost much of its value. DiBella argued that the average titleholder can walk through Times Square during rush hour without being recognized.

“We opened the door for Jake [Paul]. We opened the door for Turki Alalshikh. We opened the door for Zuffa and TKO. We opened the door for Dana and Nick. Anyone saying we didn’t open that door is a liar.”

Zuffa Boxing also has a clearer route to casual American viewers. Paramount already owns a large entertainment platform, while DAZN remains known primarily among dedicated boxing followers in the United States.

Hearn received particularly harsh criticism for his attempt to conquer the American market. DiBella described him as an effective self-promoter who can make individual events feel important, but said he returned to Britain “with his tail between his legs.”

His failure leaves Matchroom, Queensberry, Top Rank, and PBC facing a company with a stronger US television position and a centralized business model. British promoters have the best chance of remaining powerful because the UK is boxing’s strongest national market, DiBella believes, but he sees no traditional promotional company equipped to stop Zuffa in America.

The risk is that Zuffa replaces boxing’s fragmented system with a near-monopoly that controls fighters, championships, and matchmaking. DiBella dislikes that outcome, yet his larger argument is difficult to dismiss: the old guard had control of boxing and gave Zuffa every reason to believe it can run the business better.

Ghana News.title: IERPP demands answers as GoldBod reports disappear from website
Ghana News.content:
The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) is demanding answers from the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) over reports that previously published quarterly trading reports are no longer readily accessible on its website.

The Institute says the reported removal goes beyond a website management issue and raises concerns about transparency, accountability and compliance with the law governing an institution responsible for a significant part of Ghana’s gold trade.

IERPP is therefore calling on GoldBod to explain who authorised the removal of the reports, when they were taken down, why they were removed, and whether any figures contained in them were subsequently changed.

“If the reports were removed, GoldBod must tell Ghanaians who authorised their removal, when they were removed, why they were removed, and whether any figures were subsequently changed,” the Institute said.

IERPP's concerns centre on Section 42 of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which requires GoldBod to publish quarterly reports on its activities for the purposes of transparency and accountability.

The reports are required to cover areas including the Board’s operations, revenue, contracts, expenditure, as well as responsible sourcing and traceability.

The Institute further points to Section 42(2), which requires GoldBod to ensure access to reports published under the provision.

IERPP argues that the requirement therefore goes beyond simply publishing a report and requires the information to remain meaningfully accessible to the public.

The Institute says the issue is particularly important because GoldBod itself requires market participants to comply with reporting obligations.

“If reporting is important enough for GoldBod to enforce against private operators, why should Ghanaians struggle to access GoldBod's own reports?” it asked.

IERPP says public access to the reports is necessary for citizens and Parliament to scrutinise transactions involving Ghana’s gold resources and public finances.

It argues that the reports should provide information that allows the public to understand transactions, prices, contracts, fees, discounts, trading margins and the risks and costs associated with the gold purchasing programme.

According to IERPP, GoldBod’s second-quarter statutory report, covering April to June 2025, provided significant information on the Board’s operations.

The report disclosed that GoldBod purchased 26,009.56 kilogrammes of gold, equivalent to about 780,437.60 ounces, from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector at an estimated value of US$2.62 billion.

It also reported that artisanal and small-scale mining gold exports totalled 30,361.64 kilogrammes, valued at approximately US$2.99 billion.

IERPP says the disappearance of such reports could limit the public’s ability to track GoldBod’s operations and compare information released at different periods.

The issue comes amid growing scrutiny of GoldBod and Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

IERPP has previously called for a consolidated financial account of the programme following concerns over a reported US$1.7 billion loss associated with the initiative.

The Institute says such an account would allow Parliament and the public to establish how much was spent, what Ghana received in return and whether the programme ultimately generated a net benefit for the country.

The Institute is calling on GoldBod to restore all previously published quarterly reports and establish a permanent public archive.

It is also demanding that the Board:

Explain any deletion, withdrawal, amendment or replacement of previously published reports;

Publish original and revised versions where figures have changed, together with explanations for material changes;

Provide the publication and removal dates for each report; and

Ensure information required under Section 42 remains publicly accessible.

IERPP is further calling for greater disclosure of off-taker fees, trading margins, discounts, assay charges and other transaction costs to enable independent scrutiny.

The concerns come as GoldBod continues to implement reforms to Ghana’s gold purchasing and trading framework.

The Board recently said it had raised nearly US$839 million in advances for gold purchases between March and May 2026.

It has also introduced changes to the gold purchasing system, including a new pricing regime, purchase thresholds and mandatory real-time transaction reporting requirements.

GoldBod was established in April 2025 under the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), with responsibility for aggregating, assaying and exporting gold produced by licensed artisanal and small-scale mining operators.

IERPP says given the scale of GoldBod’s mandate and the public resources involved, access to statutory reports must not be treated as a discretionary matter.

“Publish the reports. Restore the archive. Explain every deletion. Open the books,” the Institute said.

It insists that transparency is a statutory obligation rather than a favour to the Ghanaian public.

Ghana News.title: Country music legend Dolly Parton dies
Ghana News.content:
Country music legend Dolly Parton, who wrote hit songs like Jolene and I Will Always Love You, has died aged 80, her family announced on social media.

Parton crossed into pop with albums like 9 to 5 and Odd Jobs (1980), tied to her starring role in the film 9 to 5.

Her business acumen shone with the 1986 opening of Dollywood, a Tennessee theme park celebrating her Appalachian roots, now a major tourist draw.

A prolific philanthropist, her Dollywood Foundation supports literacy, donating millions of books via Imagination Library.

Parton died as one of the most-honoured female country performers of all time, with her many awards including 11 Grammys and three Emmys, as well as nominations for two Academy Awards, six Golden Globe Awards and a Tony Award.

She recorded 48 studio albums throughout her lifetime, with over 100 millions records sold worldwide.

Dolly Parton's career at a glance

Long before she was known as the "Queen of Country", Dolly Parton was born in 1946 in Sevierville, Tennessee.

Raised in poverty, she began performing as a child, singing on local radio by the age of 10.

At 13, she recorded her first single, Puppy Love, and appeared at the Grand Ole Opry, a regular live country-music radio broadcast originating from Nashville, marking her early ambition.

After moving to Nashville in 1964, she gained traction as a songwriter, with hits like Put It Off Until Tomorrow covered by others.

Her breakthrough came with appearances on Porter Wagoner's long-running musical variety show (1967–1974), boosting her visibility.

Her solo career then soared with the 1974 songs Jolene and I Will Always Love You (later covered to further acclaim by Whitney Houston), showcasing her storytelling and emotional depth.

Parton postponed shows in October due to health reasons

Dolly Parton was forced to postpone her Las Vegas residency at the end of last year due to unspecified health issues.

Her sister asked fans to pray for the country singer, with Parton revealing she needed "a few procedures" to deal with ongoing "health challenges".

"Last night, I was up all night praying for my sister, Dolly," Freida Parton wrote on Facebook in October. "Many of you know she hasn't been feeling her best lately."

"Godspeed, my sissy Dolly. We all love you!"

After shocked fans took to social media expressing worry about Parton's health, Frieda said: "I want to clear something up. I didn't mean to scare anyone or make it sound so serious when asking for prayers for Dolly.

"She's been a little under the weather, and I simply asked for prayers because I believe so strongly in the power of prayer. It was nothing more than a little sister asking for prayers for her big sister."

Parton had been scheduled to perform six shows at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace in December.

Her Las Vegas stint would have been her first visit to the Strip since the 1990s, when she performed alongside her Islands In The Stream duet partner, Kenny Rogers.

Parton was also forced to pull out of a Dollywood event in September after being diagnosed with a kidney stone that she said was causing "a lot of problems".

'Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration': Full statement from Parton's family

Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, Dolly's sister, announced the death of his aunt in a post on her Instargam video.

"This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality," he says.

"As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment, but haven't truly felt it until now.

"It is an honour, an honour that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly.

"Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens."

He says Dolly "opened doors not just for me, but for her entire family to reach the potential we didn't even know was possible".

"Dolly also opened doors for generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent. By her example, we believed that anything was possible. She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the door she opened made and changed history." 'A farmer like her daddy' He says everyone has shared "beautiful memories with Dolly" over the years. "She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not. "Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy worked diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever. "Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy. He farmed the soil. She farmed songs and happiness." He adds: "Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest."

Ghana News.title: Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako writes: UK’s £39bn social housebuilding programme – Any lessons for Ghana?
Ghana News.content:
The UK government has announced a £39bn social housebuilding programme, to build 300,000 social and affordable homes across the nation. 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost £10bn. (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cnvly73jrrdo)

Meanwhile in Ghana, our government in 2012 borrowed $200 million to build 5,000 affordable housing units. As of 2026, fourteen (14) years later, our President, who was President when the loan was contracted, has recently announced that only 1,500 units would be completed by the end of 2027 (15-odd years after the loan was contracted).

No government under the 4th Republic covers itself in roses when it comes to affordable housing. How does the NPP/Akufo-Addo Administration explain why for 8 years, they could not complete the Saglemi Housing Project? How does the NDC/Mills-Mahama Administration explain why for 8 years they could not complete the affordable housing projects started by the Kufuor Administration, before commencing the Saglemi project?

If you are a citizen of these two countries, how would you feel?

•⁠ ⁠UK Government – 70,000 social and affordable homes in 10 years.

•⁠ ⁠ Ghana Government – 1,500 ‘affordable’ homes in 15 years.

If you can’t define which one is a ‘godforsaken country’, then you need help!

Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako, Accra

August 25, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Ghana targets 1,200MW new thermal power capacity by 2029 – Jinapor
Ghana News.content:
The government is pursuing the procurement of 1,200 megawatts of combined-cycle thermal power capacity, with the project expected to be completed by 2029, Minister for Energy and Green Transition John Abdulai Jinapor has disclosed.

According to Mr Jinapor, the initiative forms part of efforts to secure reliable electricity supply while reducing the cost of power generation for the country.

Speaking at the Future of Energy Conference, he said the government had taken an ambitious decision to procure the additional thermal capacity using the country’s own resources.

“We have taken an ambitious policy to procure 1,200 megawatts of thermal capacity with combined cycle on our own as a country so that it can reduce the cost of power,” he said.

The Minister said government was confident the project would be completed by 2029 and described it as a potential “game-changer” for Ghana’s energy sector.

Mr Jinapor, however, noted that Ghana would still require additional power between now and the completion of the project, saying government was therefore working on arrangements to bridge the supply gap during the transition period.

He said the additional capacity would ultimately help reduce the burden of expensive power on consumers while supporting the country’s industrialisation agenda.

The Minister stressed that Ghana’s energy sector must provide not only sufficient electricity but also reliable and affordable power capable of supporting businesses and industries.

He said the government would continue to pursue reforms and investments aimed at building a more financially sustainable and competitive electricity sector.

Ghana News.title: Ghana targets universal electricity access by 2030 as coverage nears 90%
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is targeting universal access to electricity by 2030, with the country’s electricity access rate now approaching 90 percent, Energy and Green Transition Minister John Abdulai Jinapor has announced.

The Minister said the government had recently connected an additional 200 communities to the national grid as part of efforts to close the remaining gap and extend electricity to communities still without access.

“Ghana currently has about 90% access to electricity. We just connected 200 more communities, and we are working to close the remaining gap by 2030,” Mr Jinapor said.

He was speaking at the Future of Energy Conference, where he outlined Ghana’s electricity ambitions and the need to ensure that increased access translates into reliable and affordable power.

“Our vision is that by 2030, we should achieve universal access to electricity here in Ghana,” he stated.

Mr Jinapor, however, stressed that Ghana’s electricity target should not be measured only by the number of people connected to the national grid.

He said the quality, reliability and cost of electricity would be equally important as the country seeks to expand industrial activity and create jobs.

“What kind of electricity are we providing and at what cost? With what reliability, and can it power competitive African industries?” he asked.

According to the Minister, Ghana’s industrialisation agenda will require a power supply capable of supporting businesses and industries consistently and at competitive prices.

The government is therefore seeking to address the remaining access gap while also strengthening the wider power sector.

Mr Jinapor also pointed to emerging sources of electricity demand, including the growing adoption of electric vehicles.

He said Ghana would have to strengthen its electricity infrastructure to accommodate changing consumption patterns without placing additional pressure on supply to households and businesses.

This will require investment not only in generation but also in transmission and distribution infrastructure, alongside renewable energy and energy storage systems.

The Minister's comments come as Ghana continues efforts to expand electricity access while dealing with the broader challenge of ensuring a stable power supply to support economic activity.

With about four years remaining to the 2030 target, the government faces the dual task of connecting the communities that remain without electricity and ensuring that the power supplied is reliable and affordable enough to support Ghana’s industrialisation ambitions.

Ghana News.title: Titus-Glover files nomination to contest NPP National Organiser position
Ghana News.content:
Former Tema East Member of Parliament Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover has officially filed his nomination to contest for the position of National Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

Mr Titus-Glover arrived at the party’s headquarters with a large crowd of supporters as he submitted his nomination forms for the upcoming national executive elections.

Speaking after filing his nomination, he said his campaign has already taken him across 15 regions and 229 constituencies, with plans to visit the 16th region and an additional 47 constituencies as part of his engagements with party members.

According to him, his engagements across the country have given him confidence that the NPP is poised to reclaim power in the 2028 general elections.

“The signal is clear. It is absolute. We have nothing but victory,” he declared, while referring to the prospects of the party’s flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia.

Mr Titus-Glover said the party must, however, work strategically and maintain discipline if it is to achieve its electoral objective.

“All hands are on deck. There’s a lot of work to be done. We need strategy. We need discipline, effective communication, and all the things that we need to better the work,” he said.

He also called for a peaceful political transition in 2028, drawing a comparison with the peaceful transfer of power between former President Nana Akufo-Addo and President John Dramani Mahama.

He urged the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) and President Mahama not to interfere with the will of voters in the next election.

“Just like Nana Akufo-Addo handed power to President Mahama peacefully, in 2028, President Mahama should not act funny,” he said.

Mr Titus-Glover maintained that the NPP’s return to power would ultimately be determined by Ghanaian voters.

Ghana News.title: NPP women’s organiser aspirant pledges 30% female representation
Ghana News.content:
New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Women’s Organiser aspirant, Hajia Safia, has pledged to increase the number of women representing the party in Parliament to 30 percent if elected to lead the party’s Women’s Wing.

Speaking after filing her nomination at the NPP headquarters on Tuesday, August 25, Hajia Safia said improving women’s representation in Parliament would be a major priority under her leadership.

She said the NPP currently has only 10 female Members of Parliament, a situation she believes must change if the party is to strengthen women’s participation in national decision-making.

“Looking at our current situation in Parliament, we have a minority in Parliament, and we have just 10 female MPs in Parliament. It is my ultimate priority to up the numbers,” she said.

Hajia Safia said her goal would be to ensure that women make up at least 30 per cent of the NPP’s parliamentary representation, while men account for the remaining 70 per cent.

She believes achieving the target would require a deliberate effort to identify, support, and campaign for more women who are capable of winning parliamentary seats for the party.

Kasoa among key targets

As part of her strategy, Hajia Safia identified the Kasoa parliamentary constituency as one of the seats the NPP would seek to reclaim.

She noted that the constituency had previously been represented by a woman from the NPP and said the party was determined to win the seat back.

According to her, the NPP Women’s Wing, TESCON, regional women organisers and their deputies, together with other women in the party, would be instrumental in achieving that objective.

NPP targets lost parliamentary seats

Beyond Kasoa, Hajia Safia said the NPP would target a number of constituencies it lost to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2024 general elections.

She specifically mentioned Okaikwei North, Ablekuma West, and Ayawaso West Wuogon among the seats the party intends to reclaim.

“Okaikwei North will go back and reclaim the seat. Honourable Ursula’s place will go back and reclaim the seat. Ablekuma West will go back and reclaim the seat,” she said.

She added that the NPP was determined to recover all parliamentary seats lost to its opponents in the 2024 elections.

Hajia Safia also turned her attention to the NPP’s current Members of Parliament, urging them to intensify their work ahead of the 2028 elections.

Using the analogy of borrowing and repayment, she said the party would seek to take back the seats it lost in 2024.

“Payback is December 7, 2028. We will surely come for all the seats that were borrowed from the other side.”

Her comments form part of her broader campaign agenda, which seeks to increase the number of women elected on the NPP ticket while also strengthening the party’s efforts to regain constituencies lost in the last election.

Ghana News.title: GIPA explains key changes to Ghana’s investment regime to prospective investors in Atlanta
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) has explained key changes to Ghana’s investment regime to prospective investors in Atlanta, United States of America, as part of its participation in Invest Fest 2026.

The Head of Protocol at GIPA, Manuela Adu, who led the delegation, said the new Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Act, 2026 (Act 1173), had removed the general minimum capital requirement for foreign-owned enterprises and joint ventures, except trading enterprises.

She made the disclosure on behalf of Mr Simon Madjie, Chief Executive Officer of GIPA, during an engagement with investors at the Ghana Pavilion, where the Authority presented investment opportunities and outlined changes to the country’s investment framework.

Mrs Adu said a non-citizen establishing a trading enterprise was required to invest a minimum of US$500,000 in cash as equity capital, while at least 75 per cent of the workforce must comprise skilled Ghanaians. The changes are part of the new investment framework under Act 1173.

She said the reforms were intended to make Ghana’s investment environment more attractive and flexible, particularly for investors seeking opportunities beyond traditional trading activities.

Mrs Adu also highlighted Ghana’s strategic position as a gateway to the wider African market through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), whose Secretariat is headquartered in Accra.

She said investors who established businesses in Ghana could use the country as a base to access markets across the African continent.

Mrs Adu also introduced prospective investors to GIPA’s 24-hour service for investment registrations, investment renewals and quota applications.

She said the service was designed to provide investors with timely support as they navigated the process of establishing and operating businesses in Ghana.

The engagement formed part of GIPA’s wider activities at Invest Fest, where the Authority used the Ghana Pavilion and its stage to provide information on Ghana’s investment environment and connect prospective investors with opportunities in the country.

The GIPA investment delegation comprised Principal Investment Promotion Officers, Christopher Sedor and Bridget Odei; and Assistant Public Relations Officer, Raphael Apetorgbor.

The team engaged prospective investors, responded to enquiries and provided information on Ghana’s investment opportunities, regulatory framework and available support services.

The delegation also facilitated connections between interested investors and relevant institutions, with the aim of supporting follow-up discussions and potential investment opportunities in Ghana.

GIPA said it remained available to guide investors through the investment process and facilitate their engagement with relevant institutions as they considered establishing or expanding businesses in Ghana.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
