World.title: Brown Mogotsi’s bail bid hits snag over alleged escape plan
World.content:
Oupa “Brown” Mogotsi remains in custody as his bail application on new facts continues. Image: Facebook/SABC News

Oupa “Brown” Mogotsi allegedly planned to disguise himself as a Correctional Services official and walk out of court cells in an attempt to escape custody.

The allegation emerged in the Johannesburg Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday as the 45-year-old launched another bail application based on new facts.

The court postponed proceedings to 1 September 2026 to allow Correctional Services to provide a detailed report on the alleged plot.



Official allegedly raised alarm over escape plan

During proceedings, the prosecutor read an affidavit from the investigating officer, who said a Correctional Services official alerted him that the 45-year-old was allegedly planning to escape.

Authorities subsequently put measures in place to prevent this from happening.

NPA spokesperson Magaboke Mohlatlole said the requested report would provide further details about the alleged plot.



“The postponement will allow Correctional Services to provide the court with a detailed report regarding an alleged escape plan involving Mogotsi, which was allegedly intercepted by correctional authorities,” Mohlatlole said.

JUST IN | The state has alleged that self-proclaimed political fixer Brown Mogotsi plotted an escape from court cells. pic.twitter.com/Mvsh1NzoDC — SABC News (@SABCNews) August 25, 2026

Mogotsi remains in custody.



Charges linked to Vosloorus incident

Mogotsi faces charges of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition, discharging a firearm in a built-up area, defeating or obstructing the administration of justice, and perjury.

The charges relate to an incident on 3 November 2025, when Mogotsi allegedly told police that occupants of a bakkie pursued him while he drove alone in Vosloorus.

He claimed they fired several shots at his vehicle, forcing him to stop and flee on foot.



The NPA said it would continue placing relevant information before the court as the case proceeds.

World.title: 'I withdraw' - Dlamini-Zuma retracts remarks against Lamola
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - ANC NEC member Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma has retracted remarks she made on an episode of the African Renaissance Podcast, hosted by Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, against Ronald Lamola.

In the interview, she accused Lamola and ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula of participating in vote-buying during the ANC’s 2017 and 2022 National Conferences.

READ | Lamola fires back at Dlamini-Zuma over vote-buying claims

Dlamini-Zuma alleged that a circulating audio recording directly implicated Lamola in these transactional activities.

But on Tuesday afternoon, she took to social media, where she withdrew her remarks.

"During my participation in the African Renaissance Podcast, I attributed a voice note to comrade Ronald Lamola. Comrade Lamola has since advised me that the voice was not his. I withdraw the attribution on the basis of his clarification." "The broader concern I raised regarding the influence of money in leadership contests remains an important matter that must be addressed for the renewal and integrity of the African National Congress," Dlamini-Zuma penned.

In the post, she did not mention any retraction to Mbalula.

World.title: Accused in Zolani Tete murder remain in custody
World.content:
MDANTSANE - The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) has welcomed the arrest of four men linked to the murder of renowned South African boxer Zolani Tete.

The NPA spokesperson, Luxolo Tyali, said the ‘ball is in the court of the prosecution '.

“This is to ensure that they present a formidable case both during the application for bail.” he said.

Tete, 38, was attacked on Friday evening as he returned to his home in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape.

A 27-year-old woman who was with him in the car survived but is in hospital, police said.

Alleged hitmen Siphesihle Kolisa and Athandwa Gangala, as well as alleged middleman Sinebongo Qase, were joined in court by alleged mastermind Uzuzole Goqwana, who made his first appearance on Monday.

According to the NPA, Qase and Goqwana are expected to return to the Mdantsane Magistrates' Court on 1 September 2026 for their formal bail application.

Meanwhile, Kolisa and Gangala have since abandoned their bail applications.

World.title: State says Brown Mogotsi planned to escape
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The State says political fixer Brown Mogotsi planned to escape from court during his appearance on 20 August 2026.



This emerged from Mogotsi's fourth bail bid at the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court.



Mogotsi faces charges linked to an alleged staged assassination attempt in November 2025 in Vosloorus.



The North West political fixer is charged with unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition,

perjury and defeating the ends of justice.



The state has also previously raised concerns about witness intimidation and protecting their identities.



It's alleged that Mogotsi's wife visited one of the witnesses after their address was revealed.

World.title: A passion for sports cars: How Matlala and Maumela's friendship blossomed
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala has detailed his relationship with Hangwani Maumela, a central figure in the alleged looting of Tembisa Hospital.

Matlala told the Madlanga Commission that their shared passion for luxury sports cars brought them together in 2015 or 2016.

“We both have a passion for sports cars,” he told the Madlanga Commission.

“There is a restaurant in Sandton that we both frequented. We used to meet each other there. I liked his car, and that’s how we started our relationship.”

He conceded that he and Maumela were friends and said they later entered a joint business venture, pooling funds and sharing profits from government tenders they secured.

Asked by evidence leader Advocate Sello Mahlape SC whether they had any other relationship that allowed them to benefit financially, Matlala said they did.

He told the commission that they were involved in a joint business venture in which they invested money and shared profits from government tenders they successfully secured.

Matlala did not list the projects they had secured, saying there were many.

World.title: Customary marriage registration deadline fast approaching
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Couples married in terms of customary law who have not yet registered their marriages have until 31 August to do so.

Under the Recognition of Customary Marriages Act, customary marriages have the same legal recognition and protection as civil marriages.

Couples whose marriages were concluded before 2000, as well as those married after 2000, are required to register them.

Sanlam Trust’s Adv Sankie Morata says registration is important when it comes to proving the existence of a marriage during a life-changing event.

"In the past it has become difficult to prove the existence of a particular marriage in a death or divorce," he said.

Morata says couples who have not yet registered their marriage should visit their nearest Home Affairs office.

Who must register?

World.title: LIVESTREAM | 'Cat' Matlala back for more grilling
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala returns to the stand at the Madlanga Commission on Tuesday.

Matlala resumed his testimony on Monday after proceedings were delayed by his legal team.

READ | Matlala denies close ties with other cartel suspects

During his testimony, the tender don denied having a close relationship with suspended deputy police commissioner General Shadrack Sibiya.

He told the Commission that Sibiya was not his friend, but simply “someone that I knew”.

He also insisted that he had no personal or professional relationship with alleged Big 5 Cartel member Ignatius Mothakathi.

World.title: WATCH: Ramaphosa delivers keynote address at SIDSSA 2026
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - President Cyril Ramaphosa will deliver a keynote address at the Infrastructure Symposium.

Delegates are meeting in Cape Town to find ways of accelerating investment and improve delivery across the continent.

The gathering has brought together government, business and investors to unlock infrastructure funding for major projects.

World.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
World.content:
LONDON - Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

- Only a few transits per day -

Before Iran blocked the strait in response to joint US-Israeli strikes in February, around one fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports passed through the waterway.

Iran's Guards have also warned of a "danger zone" covering 1,400 square kilometres where mines may be present.

World.title: Gachagua to Duale: You don't own pastoralists
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and delegates from Isiolo and Marsabit at Wamunyoro, Nyeri County on August 25, 2026. [Ali Abdi, Standard]

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) Leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale of allegedly doing nothing for pastoralist communities in the country.

Mr Gachagua said Duale, while being the only CS from northern Kenya and claiming to be the spokesperson of the group, had instead been a liability to pastoralists.

“You, the Borana who are here, along with the Turkana and Somali, are all complaining like other Kenyans. You suffer from runaway insecurity and widespread underdevelopment. We must join hands to vote out this rogue government (in next year's general election),” the former Deputy President told a delegation of grassroots leaders and residents from Isiolo and Marsabit who paid him a courtesy call at his Wamunyoro rural home in Nyeri.

“Duale thinks that the pastoralists are his property, his children or servants. What has he done for the people of Isiolo and Marsabit? (He has) only rhetoric, shouting pastoralists everywhere, every day,” he said.

Gachagua questioned how Duale would be able to marshal ‘millions’ of votes for President Ruto in the 2027 General Elections while he (Duale) could only raise 7,000 votes for the UDA presidential candidate in the 2022 polls in his Garissa Township Constituency backyard.

Despite his little contribution to the Kenya Kwanza administration's victory, Gachagua said Duale was appointed as the only CS from northern Kenya but had ended up doing nothing for the region and pastoralist communities.

“He only gave him (Ruto) 7,000 votes in Garissa Township. It's Central Kenya that propelled this government,” Gachagua told the gathering.

“Duale was appointed CS and he has nothing to show apart from empty words, going round shouting (the name of) pastoralists, and you (the pastoralists) are suffering. If you love them, then why are their livestock stolen every day?” He asked the CS.

“These pastoralists are killed every day and their cows and goats stolen. What have you done for them and you are in the government?” Gachagua posed.

The Opposition leader claimed that the government was ill-prepared for the heavily forecasted El Niño rainfall, pointing out that those living in flood-prone areas like the Tana Delta and Garissa are exposed to danger.

“Now, going into El Niño, what plan has been put in place to save people from death as a result of floods and how livestock will survive?” he asked the State.

During the event, Gachagua revealed that Yusuf Huka Jillo from Isiolo would represent Upper Eastern at the DCP secretariat and serve as a member of the National Executive Committee (NEC) in an acting capacity.

Gachagua said the mountain was now complete, with Isiolo and Marsabit forming Mt Kenya North.

The locals alleged that the Health CS was interfering in Isiolo County politics, with elder Hussein Jama claiming that Duale and the Office of the DCI were shielding a section of leaders accused of corruption and criminal activities.

Speakers claimed that there was massive corruption at the local lands registry office, while Mr Jillo faulted the State for the slow pace of registration of community land in Isiolo.

Jama said Isiolo International Airport, which was constructed during the administration of President Kibaki to help in the export of miraa and horticultural goods from the Mt Kenya region and livestock products, mainly meat and hides, lies idle because the expansion of the runway from 1.5 metres to 3 metres had not been done.

In response, Gachagua said the airport was meant to create employment and wealth, but the Kenya Kwanza administration had instead left it in ruin deliberately, claiming the move was aimed at sabotaging the economy of Mt Kenya and pastoralists’ economies.

“What was the good about destroying the Imenti forest to construct an airstrip for an individual while there is an international airport meant partly to serve the entire region just a few kilometres from Meru town?” Asked the DCP leader.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Liberia once offered Black Americans a new home. Decades on, it is receiving migrants the US wants out
World.content:
Is Liberia an American dumping ground — or a place where a new generation of arrivals can build a new life?

That’s the question Liberians are asking themselves after the first people to be deported to the West African country from the United States arrived in the capital, Monrovia.

The 20 people on the flight from Louisiana were the first to be sent under an agreement that could see up to 1,200 people transferred to Liberia, a country of less than 6 million people, many of them descendants of formerly enslaved Black Americans.

Liberian officials said the new arrivals were from “African and western hemisphere countries.”

Liberia is one of several countries that have agreed to take migrants being deported from the US under the Trump administration’s anti-immigration crackdown. The arrivals are coming to a nation whose history is deeply tied to migration from the US.

Nearly two centuries ago, free and formerly enslaved Black Americans crossed the Atlantic to settle in what would become Liberia – a name that translates as “land of the free.”

Now, a country shaped in part by that migration is accepting people the US wants to remove.

For Liberians, that has thrown up a mix of feelings in a country still recovering from a long and bloody civil war.

“This country is going through a lot, and having more people come in — can we handle all of this?” said Pheta Morris, 48, a descendant of the Black Americans who settled in Liberia.

A plane carrying the deportees from the US arrives at the Roberts International Airport outside of Monrovia, Liberia, on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Alexander Wiaplah/AP

But she said she sees the new arrivals through the lens of Liberia’s history and is struck by the contrast.

“I think about the Americo-Liberians — people who were rejected where they were and needed somewhere to go, and Liberia opened its arms to them,” she said.

“Back then, people needed somewhere they could be free, accepted and welcomed. Now, people are being rejected from the US, and Liberia is opening its doors to them.”

The first transfer has already faced complications.

Reuters reported that five migrants who refused to disembark after arriving in Monrovia were flown instead to Equatorial Guinea in Central Africa, where they are held with more than 30 other migrants previously sent there by the US.

A US State Department spokesperson said implementing the Trump administration’s immigration policies was a “top priority,” adding that the department generally does not comment on private diplomatic communications with other governments.

CNN has contacted Liberia’s information ministry for more details about the agreement and its terms.

A country shaped by America

The first group of free Black Americans arrived in Liberia in the early 1820s.

Over the following decades, thousands more made the journey, with the American Colonization Society helping to establish settlements along the West African coast. The US State Department says about 16,000 Black Americans migrated to Liberia during the 19th century.

The members of the Liberian senate of 1893, mostly made up of freed African American slaves, posing together for a group portrait. Library of Congress/Corbis/VCG/Getty Images

The migration was complicated. Some Black Americans saw Liberia as a chance to escape racism and build a new life, while others opposed the colonization movement and rejected the idea that free Black people should leave the US.

Africans rescued from slave ships by the US Navy were also brought to Liberia. The settlements eventually formed the Republic of Liberia, which declared independence in 1847.

The American influence remains visible today. Liberia’s flag resembles that of the US; its capital was named Monrovia after America’s fifth President James Monroe, and its early institutions were heavily influenced by Washington.

Conmany Wesseh, a former Liberian lawmaker and member of the ruling Unity Party who was nominated as Liberia’s ambassador to the United Nations and later the European Union under former president Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, said that history continues to shape how Liberians view the US.

For Wesseh though, the arrival of the deportees raises a more immediate question: Can Liberia, a country still struggling with basic infrastructure and services, accommodate more people?

The cost of taking them in

Liberia began rebuilding after a 14-year civil war ended in 2003, but Wesseh said the country still needs major investment. Poverty levels remain high and youth unemployment stands at 40%, according to African Development Bank data.

“Our country needs a great deal of support,” he said. “We are short on medical facilities, and we have problems with education.”

He questioned how the country would manage an influx of people from abroad.

“They will have to go to the same hospitals. You won’t create a new hospital for them,” he said. “There’s no spare housing. We don’t have existing housing to put new people in.”

Wide view of Monrovia, Liberia, from the top of the Ducor Hotel, on June 15, 2025. (AP Photo/Annie Risemberg, File Annie Risemberg/AP

Wesseh said Liberia’s development needs may have influenced the government’s decision, with officials hoping the agreement would bring support from Washington.

Liberian authorities described the arrangement as humanitarian and said the deportees will be treated as guests who can seek asylum or leave the country.

Asked whether he viewed the deal as humanitarian assistance, a diplomatic arrangement or the US outsourcing its immigration enforcement, Wesseh chose the latter.

“I think (the administration of US President Donald Trump) just sees this as a place to dump people,” he said. “They want to take them off their hands and dump them in this country.”

A chance for a new start

Francis Dennis had long known that his family had roots in the migration of Black Americans to Liberia in the 19th century. But just a few weeks ago, he became curious about his family’s past and began using AI genealogy tools to dig deeper into that history.

The 71-year-old former president of the Liberia Chamber of Commerce told CNN he traced his great-great-great-grandfather to Snow Hill, a town on Maryland’s Eastern Shore in the US, using the technology and notes left by his father.

He said the research also pointed him to the name of the vessel that carried his ancestor across the Atlantic to Liberia, along with a list of its passengers.

Generations later, Dennis is watching another group arrive in Liberia from the US. But he does not believe their circumstances have to define what comes next.

“People may have their apprehension about a new life, but it’s also an opportunity,” he said. “Some may be happy, some may resent it, but it opens a new window, a new opportunity.”

His own ancestor crossed the Atlantic generations ago and became part of the community that helped shape modern Liberia.

Now, he hopes those arriving under very different circumstances will also see the country as a chance for a fresh start.

“The ball will be in their court,” Dennis said. “Are they going to seize it as an opportunity for a new start, a fresh start, a new life? Or will they be thinking about the past?”

World.title: US is “not in a position” to limit economic relations, Iran’s top negotiator says
World.content:
After US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened new sanctions targeting countries with ties to Iran, top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf argued that the US is not in an economic position to restrict its relations with other countries.

“The Americans know that no one believes their bluster. Economically, the United States is not in a position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” Ghalibaf said.

Ghalibaf, Iran’s parliamentary speaker, wrote in a post on X that “Iran’s trading partners have stated — both publicly in the media and in messages sent to us — that they attach no importance to these remarks.”

Meanwhile, Iran’s semi-official Tasnim News Agency quoted a senior Iranian intelligence source as claiming the new US measures were aimed primarily at influencing public opinion rather than imposing meaningful new restrictions.

The source said the measures were “based solely on the design of Trump’s media team” and were intended to increase “psychological pressure on the people of Iran,” Tasnim added, without naming the source.

World.title: OpenAI subpoenaed by Alabama attorney general over Hugging Face hack
World.content:
Alabama’s attorney general on Monday subpoenaed OpenAI for more information related to its AI agents autonomously hacking into another company’s servers in July.

The subpoena is part of an investigation into whether OpenAI’s practices “violated Alabama’s consumer protection laws” and pose a risk to Alabama citizens, the attorney general’s office said in a statement.

Last month, OpenAI disclosed that during a test of its AI models’ capabilities on cybersecurity, the agents autonomously escaped the lab environment and hacked Hugging Face, an online platform for AI models and data sets, to obtain the answer to the test.

“This AI lab leak showed that Alabamians’ and Americans’ worst fears about artificial intelligence are not just theoretical. Our investigation seeks to uncover the facts and address hard truths about the threats companies and consumers are facing from rogue AI,” Attorney General Steve Marshall said in the statement.

OpenAI called the Hugging Face hack “unprecedented,” and the company’s president, Greg Brockman, said the incident “showed that we underestimated the real-world cyber capabilities of our AI models.” OpenAI halted some of its AI model training and is hardening its testing, monitoring and training protocols following the incident.

“The Hugging Face incident marked an important moment for AI safety and we are conducting a thorough review along with external advisors,” an OpenAI spokesperson told CNN on Monday. “Once the review is complete, we will share a technical report with relevant government authorities and publish our findings publicly.”

Monday’s subpoena calls for OpenAI to document its safety protocols and model behavior records as well as ascertain all damages caused by the hack, in addition to other information.

Alabama, along with 14 other Republican states’ attorneys general, sent a letter earlier this month to OpenAI demanding the company preserve information and documents related to the Hugging Face hack.

The problem of autonomous agents going rogue isn’t limited to OpenAI — Meta and Anthropic also disclosed their own systems took unsanctioned actions during cybersecurity tests, a wake-up call for the AI and cybersecurity industry.

OpenAI faces a litany of lawsuits and investigations by various states. This includes cases related to its engagement algorithms, handling of consumer and health data, model “sycophancy,” and its marketing strategies directed at minors and senior citizens. In June, Florida became the first state to sue OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, alleging the company knows ChatGPT is not safe for minors.

World.title: Iranian media reports long lines and temporary closures at gas stations in Tehran
World.content:
Drivers in the Iranian capital of Tehran are experiencing long lines at gas stations and temporary fuel shortages, according to Iranian news agencies, although authorities have insisted the overall fuel supply chain remains stable.

It comes as US strikes on Iranian oil storage infrastructure, the US blockade and fears of rising inflation are believed to be triggering fuel shortages and subsequent rushes on gas stations.

Iranian news agency Rokna reported that people in Tehran said some petrol stations had no gas available, forcing them to temporarily close, while other stations had long lines on Monday and Tuesday.

Tabnak, another news agency, published a similar report on Monday, saying it received comments from readers who were experiencing restricted fuel availability in eastern and southern Tehran.

Social media users in Tehran also reported gas stations without petrol in more urban, northern neighborhoods. And outside of the capital, reports of diesel and gas shortages in Mazandaran province and Fars province have emerged on social media. CNN is unable to independently verify those reports.

The National Iranian Oil Products Distribution Company (NIOPDC) has said the country’s fuel supply chain remains stable, and the shortages and long lines are being caused by rumors that lead to panic buying, as well as delays in fuel deliveries. The distribution company said the issue “should be resolved within the next few days,” according to Rokna.

The Tehran region director of the NIOPDC also said that damage inflicted on Tehran’s petroleum product storage and distribution infrastructure during the war has created some constraints on fuel distribution.

World.title: PM follows up with CBE governor on joint coordination efforts in several economic files
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed full coordination between the government and the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) as part of preparations for the National Economic Transformation Program, based on an integrated vision reflecting the state’s economic priorities for the coming period.

This is being carried out in implementation of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s directives and aims to ensure the integration of economic, fiscal, monetary, and sectoral policies and measures, while achieving a tangible impact on the national economy.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting on Monday, August 24, 2026, with CBE Governor Hassan Abdalla at the government headquarters in New Alamein City.

The meeting was held as part of regular coordination between the government and CBE to follow up on priority economic issues and discuss mechanisms for strengthening financial and monetary stability.

The meeting reviewed several issues related to the performance of the Egyptian economy during the current period, including coordination efforts to continue reducing inflation rates, efforts to increase dollar inflows, indicators related to strengthening the state’s foreign currency reserves, and economic and structural reforms.

The meeting also confirmed that Egypt has safe levels of foreign currency reserves capable of securing the country’s strategic needs for essential commodities.

Continuous efforts are being made to strengthen strategic stocks of various commodities through ongoing coordination between the government and the Central Bank in this regard.

For his part, Abdalla said that the CBE Board of Directors had approved the regulations governing services under the Digital Financial Identity System, which enables banks to identify customers and electronically verify their identities.

The move comes as part of the bank’s ongoing efforts to support digital transformation and promote financial inclusion, in line with the Egyptian state’s vision of transitioning to digital financial services.

He explained that the regulations establish an integrated regulatory framework for services under the Digital Financial Identity System, covering governance of the system and defining the roles and responsibilities of all participating parties, as well as technical and operational requirements, data protection controls, and cybersecurity measures.

This is intended to ensure that services are delivered according to the highest standards of security and efficiency and in line with international best practices.

World.title: Egypt, Mongolia discuss cooperation in water resources management
World.content:
Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Hani Sewilam discussed with Mongolian Minister of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry Tsagaankhuugiin Iderbat ways to enhance cooperation and exchange expertise in water resources management, amid growing challenges facing the water and agriculture sectors and the importance of sound water resources management in supporting food security and sustainable development.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of Sewilam’s participation in the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17) in Mongolia.

Sewilam outlined the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation’s vision for implementing the second generation of Egypt’s water management system (2.0), which seeks to develop water management through integrating engineering and technological solutions, improving water-use efficiency and expanding reliance on modern technologies in managing water resources.

The two sides also underscored the importance of maximizing the return on each unit of water and improving water-use efficiency, particularly in agriculture.

World.title: Egypt overtakes Spain, France, Croatia, Serbia in Taranto 2026 medal standings
World.content:
Egyptian teams competing at the Mediterranean Games in Taranto continued their strong performances, winning medals and propelling Egypt past Spain, France, Croatia and Serbia in the overall medal standings.

In sport, some athletes compete simply to make up the numbers, while others seek to leave their mark in the history books.

In Taranto, Egypt is not merely competing for numbers, it is showcasing a new philosophy: what matters is not how many athletes a delegation brings, but how many champions can carry their country’s flag to the podium.

This has been the story of Egypt at the Mediterranean Games, where the Pharaohs have climbed to fifth place in the medal table with 13 medals, surpassing major sporting powers including Spain, France, Croatia and Serbia.

Egypt has also maintained its position at the top of the Arab medal standings, five medals ahead of Tunisia.

Perhaps the most significant figure, however, is not the 13 medals but the number that preceded it: 196. That is the number of Egyptian athletes competing at the Games, compared with much larger delegations numbering more than 300 or even 400 athletes.

Italy has 498 athletes, Turkey 334, France 330, Greece 281, Algeria 268 and Spain 249.

So far, Egypt’s medals have come from three main sports, swimming, fencing and wrestling, highlighting the depth and diversity of Egyptian sport and its ability to produce champions across multiple disciplines.

Behind this performance is close coordination among Olympic champion and Minister of Youth and Sports Gohar Nabil, Egyptian Olympic Committee President Yasser Idris, and the national sports federations, based on a simple but challenging principle: Egypt does not need the largest delegation; it needs the strongest delegation.

Minister Gohar Nabil was keen to be present alongside the athletes, providing support and encouragement during his attendance at the opening ceremony.

Meanwhile, Yasser Idris overcame his grief following the death of his mother, which coincided with the start of the competitions and caused him to arrive in Italy later than planned, in order to support the Egyptian delegation and follow its performances.

Egypt’s 13 medals have placed the country firmly among the leading nations and kept it at the top of the Arab standings, with four gold, four silver and five bronze medals, as follows:

Swimming

Gold: Abdelrahman Sameh — 50m butterfly

Bronze: Farida Osman — 50m butterfly

Bronze: Youssef Ramadan — 100m butterfly

Fencing

Gold: Mohamed al-Sayed — épée

Gold: Mohamed Hamza — foil

Silver: Sara Hosny — foil

Silver: Youssef Shamel — épée

Bronze: Abdelrahman Tolba — foil

Wrestling

Gold: Mohamed Hassan — 67kg

Silver: Mahmoud Farag — 60kg

Silver: Abdelrahman Haitham — 125kg

Bronze: Mostafa Hussein — 77kg

Bronze: Shehab al-Din Abdel-Raouf — 65kg

World.title: Irrigation minister: Egypt pursuing an integrated approach to maximize efficient use of available water resources
World.content:
Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Hani Sewilam affirmed that Egypt is pursuing an integrated approach to maximize the efficient use of its available water resources by improving water-use efficiency, expanding the reuse of agricultural drainage water and optimizing the use of every drop of water, particularly in light of the country’s limited water resources and growing demand.

Sewilam made the remarks during a lecture titled “Innovations in Water Resources Management,” delivered on the sidelines of his participation in the 17th Session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17), being held in Mongolia.

During the lecture, the minister outlined the main features of Egypt’s water resources system and reviewed the country’s water resources and needs, as well as measures being implemented to strengthen water security and ensure sustainable management of available resources.

Sewilam also highlighted Egypt’s efforts to deepen cooperation with Nile Basin countries and other African nations, stressing that Egypt attaches great importance to regional cooperation as a means of advancing sustainable development and promoting the exchange of expertise and knowledge in water resources management, in a manner that serves the common interests of African peoples.

The minister outlined the main pillars of the second generation of Egypt’s water management system (Water 2.0), with a particular focus on rehabilitating and upgrading water infrastructure and deploying advanced technologies to enhance the management and operation of the water system.

He noted that the ministry is expanding the use of satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) for monitoring and surveillance, enabling the collection of accurate, real-time data and enhancing decision-making capabilities.

Sewilam also presented Egypt’s digital twin project for the Ismailia Canal as a pioneering example of applying advanced technology to water management.

The project represents a significant step toward the digital transformation of the water system by integrating data and modern technologies into the monitoring and management of water resources and improving operational efficiency.

The minister further reviewed the state’s efforts to treat and reuse agricultural drainage water, describing the initiative as a key component of Egypt’s strategy to maximize the use of available water resources.

He also highlighted ongoing efforts to protect Egypt’s coastlines through environmentally friendly materials and nature-based solutions, helping mitigate the increasing impacts of climate change and safeguard vulnerable coastal areas.

Sewilam underscored the importance of good governance and institutional capacity-building in water resources management.

He pointed to the ministry’s efforts to strengthen the participation of water users through the establishment and support of Water User Associations, while also enhancing communication with members of the House of Representatives and the Senate.

These efforts, he said, promote greater coordination among the ministry, water users and legislative institutions in addressing water-related challenges.

The minister also highlighted a pioneering initiative launched by the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation to train rural women in using water hyacinth to produce handicrafts. The initiative seeks to turn an environmental challenge into an opportunity for economic empowerment, income generation and job creation.

Sewilam affirmed that Egypt will continue to modernize and strengthen its water management system by integrating modern infrastructure, advanced technology, water reuse, nature-based solutions, sound governance and community participation under the second generation of the national water management system.

This integrated approach, he stressed, is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of Egypt’s water resources, strengthening water security and supporting the country’s broader development objectives.

World.title: Driver dies in Kazungula accident
World.content:
A 32-year-old man identified as Andrew Edwin Simwimba of Kabanana Site and Service, Lusaka who was a driver for City Frontiers in Lusaka died yesterday in Kazungula after being run over by an unknown truck.

The accident which claimed the life of the victim occurred between 04:00 hours and 07:00 hours at the Kazungula Bridge Point Truck Park on August 24, 2026.

Mr Simwimba sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced dead upon arrival at Kazungula District Hospital and his body has been taken to Batoka Hospital Mortuary in Livingstone awaiting post-mortem examination.

This is according to a statement issued by Southern Province Commanding Officer, Moono Namalongo.

Mr Namalongo disclosed that preliminary investigations indicate that the pedestrian, who was reportedly under the influence of alcohol or drugs, was lying in the truck park when he was run over by an unknown truck bearing an unknown registration number and being driven by an unknown driver.

“The circumstances surrounding the accident are subject to further investigation. The Zambia Police Service is appealing to the driver involved or anyone with information that may assist in identifying the vehicle and driver to report to the nearest police station,” Mr Namalongo said.

World.title: Chinsali Council relocates roadside traders
World.content:
The Lamba Lima Council of Elders has congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election as Republican President.

Council of Elders Member, Josphat Nsundwe, says the victory obtained in the August 13, 2026 general elections has cheered the Lamba people on the Copperbelt Province and other areas.

Mr Nsundwe said the Lamba people on the Copperbelt, Central and Northwestern Provinces have praised President Hichilema for winning another term in office.

He added that the Council of Elders has noted a number of projects that the President has undertaken in the past five years.

Mr Nsundwe said programmes such as free education have seen a number of children going back to school.

He added that the school feeding programme, is also helping in improving the lives of school going children.

World.title: IBA renews 16 broadcasting licenses
World.content:
The Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) Board has renewed sixteen broadcasting licenses across the country.

The renewed licenses include 14 radio stations and two in the television category, comprising seven community radio stations, six commercial and two religious stations respectively.

And the Board has approved applications for three broadcasters to change their licence categories and station names.

IBA Director General Webster Malido disclosed this in a press statement issued today.

Mr Malido said the renewals and approvals were granted during its 46th Ordinary Board Meeting held recently.

He said that the approvals and renewals of the licenses are a statutory and regulatory requirement in accordance with Section 28 of the Independent Broadcasting Authority (Amendment) Act No. 26 of 2010.

He named the stations whose licenses were renewed as Shekinah Community Radio of Chingola district, Namwianga Community Radio in Kalomo, Salvation Army Radio in Chikankata, Breeze FM Radio in Chipata, Kwenje Community Radio in Chama and Nyimba FM Radio.

Others are PASME Community Radio of Petauke, 945 Metro Sports Radio of Lusaka, Tuta FM Radio in Mansa, Bangweula FM Radio in Samfya, Direct Connect Talk Radio in Lusaka, Kokoliko Radio in Chingola, Kanchibiya FM Radio in Kanchibiya and Chipata’s Radio Maria.

Lumen Television and Strong Technologies Subscription Management Service both of Lusaka are in the television category.

Mr Malido, who also serves as Board Secretary, said all renewed licenses are valid for a period of five years, subject to payment of prescribed fees and continued compliance with the IBA Act, broadcasting guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures.

He stated that the Authority reminds all broadcasting licensees that applications for license renewal, together with all required documentation and prescribed fees, should be submitted at least six months before the expiry of their licenses in accordance with the law.

Meanwhile, the Board, pursuant to Section 27 of the Independent Broadcasting Authority (Amendment) Act No. 26 of 2010, approved applications by three broadcasters to change their broadcasting license categories.

Chisamba FM was approved to change its broadcasting licence category from Community to Commercial, while Blessings Miracle Television and Miracle FM Radio changed from Religious Community to Commercial categories.

Mr Malido revealed that Chisamba FM in Chisamba district changed its name to Mwomboshi FM while Blessings Miracle Television in Lusaka district also changed its name to Beacon Media Television.

He said the IBA reiterates its commitment to promoting a professional, diverse and accessible broadcasting sector in the country.

He urged all broadcasting licensees to continue operating in compliance with their licence conditions, the IBA Act, broadcasting regulations, guidelines and programming standards.

World.title: Mwense Hospital gets new children’s ward
World.content:
Government has commissioned a 25 bed capacity children’s ward at Mwense District Hospital constructed under capital projects infrastructure development.

Mwense District Commissioner, Happystone Mwape, who commissioned the ward, said the facility is part of the government’s broader commitment to improving the quality of health services.

Mr Mwape said government’s determination to improve the quality of health services includes expansion of infrastructure, improved working environment for health workers and accessible medical attention to all citizens.

He urged the hospital administrative team and health workers to ensure that the hospital infrastructure including the new children’s ward are maintained.

Mr Mwape thanked the residents of Mwense District for being patient as the ward was being constructed.

“As government, we know that there are so many needs that need attention but we need to celebrate the progress made,” he said.

And receiving the ward on behalf of the Ministry of Health, Mwense Town Council Secretary, Dulani Phiri thanked the government saying the ward had come at a time when there was need to improve health services for the children.

Mr Phiri added the construction of the children’s ward is an indication of government’s commitment to improving access to quality health services for the citizens.

“The commissioning of this ward is a major milestone in improving healthcare as government strived to enhance child health,” he said.

Meanwhile, residents who witnessed the handover ceremony, expressed delight saying the children’s ward will help promote the dignity of children as they access health services.

A resident, Lazarus Mulenga, narrated that previously, children could be mixed with adults in wards, a situation he described as unconducive.

“Before the ward was constructed, children could be mixed with adults in admission wards and I feel that situation posed a danger to their already ill health,” he said.

World.title: Education authorities urged to implement quality education
World.content:
Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary, Tuesday Bwalya, has challenged education authorities in the area to ensure effective implementation of quality education.

Dr Bwalya says it is important to ensure that key government policies in the sector such as free education, school feeding programmes and the provision of adequate desks in schools, are effectively implemented to enhance delivery of quality education.

He said this when he held a meeting with the Provincial Education Officer, District Education Board Secretaries and Education Standards Officers from across the Province.

He reminded them to adhere to the presidential directive of seeing no child sitting on the floor while learning as a starting point to achieve quality education.

Dr Bwalya emphasised the need for this directive to be followed saying he will be inspecting schools to see if this Presidential directive is being adhered to.

“I will be making impromptu visits to schools to check on availability of desks in schools, and check on how programmes such as the school feeding programme is being executed,” he said.

He also challenged authorities to use part of the grants they are receiving from government to implement the directive.

“I know that the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), is not enough to procure desks as it has so many components, but we can use the money we are receiving from the Ministry of Education to also budget for procurement of desks to supplement what CDF is offering,” he said.

Dr Bwalya has encouraged Education managers as implementers of Government policies to read and understand the UPND manifesto to ensure provision of quality education during the party’s five year mandate.

“The free education, quality education and school feeding programme should move in line with goals set in the UPND manifesto,” he said.

He stated that government has been providing funding to schools in good time adding that going forward the school grants will be revised.

And speaking during the same meeting, Muchinga Province Education Officer, Alexander Mulenga appreciated the engagement with the Permanent Secretary and implored on District Education Board Secretaries and Education Standards Officers to work hard and support the Government of the day.

Mr Mulenga said all raised concerns on sanitation in schools and school feeding programmes among others will be looked into.

“As Ministry of Education in Muchinga Province, we want to push for more school infrastructure and ensure schools have good sanitation,” he said

World.title: State House dismisses HH involvement in Court closures
World.content:
State House has dismissed claims that President Hakainde Hichilema directed the closure of courts yesterday Monday, August 24, 2026, to prevent opposition political parties from filing in election petitions.

In a statement made available to the media, State House Chief Communications Specialist Clayson Hamasaka says President Hichilema remains committed to good governance, the rule of law and the principle of separation of powers.

Mr Hamasaka says the Judiciary is an independent arm of government and that the Head of State

Mr Hamasaka has explained that the measures taken yesterday followed security risk assessments conducted at selected government premises across the country, including institutions under the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security, the National Prosecution Authority and the Attorney General’s Chambers.

He said the allegations were inconsistent with the constitution and the facts surrounding the temporary suspension of operations at selected government institutions.

He said the operations were intelligence-led and were preventive measures aimed at protecting government institutions, public officers and members of the public accessing the premises.

He stated that security measures affected several government departments and arms of government and could therefore not be interpreted as targeting any individual or party seeking legal recourse.

The Chief Communication Specialist further noted that the temporary suspension of court operations was not unprecedented, citing similar measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic when court sittings were restricted in the interest of public safety.

Mr Hamasaka reiterated that the government remains committed to upholding judicial independence and ensuring that all state institutions operate within their constitutional mandates.

World.title: Political leaders re-echo call for national peace
World.content:
A Senior Government official in Mpulungu District has called on stakeholders to support the success of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II project.

Mpulungu District Commissioner Gehard Sikazwe says the project should be supported by relevant stakeholders for it to bring about socio-economic development of the district.

Mr Sikazwe disclosed that the project has the potential to significantly improve the living standards of people and boost local economic activities in Mpulungu and the surrounding areas.

Speaking during the District Development Coordinating Committee meeting, Mr Sikazwe explained that the Tralard II project is part of the broader national development agenda which focuses on enhancing social amenities and promoting sustainable livelihoods.

“This project is designed to create opportunities for local residents, especially in the areas of small-scale enterprises and cooperatives. this is why community participation and stakeholder support are vital for the project,” he explained

Mr Sikazwe has since urged stakeholders to ensure that the project benefits the most vulnerable groups and marginalized populations in Mpulungu.

TRALARD II Project District Operations Officer James Chilufya reaffirmed the project’s commitment to helping the community with necessary support that will make them realise the full benefit of the project.

Mr Chilufya emphasised that shared responsibility among all stakeholders is essential for overcoming challenges that the project might face and maximizing the project’s impact.

He assured stakeholders that adequate resources and technical assistance would be provided to facilitate smooth implementation.

Mr Chilufya has also called on stakeholders to share their expertise and innovative ideas to enhance the project’s effectiveness.

He said with strong community involvement and strategic partnerships, the initiative is poised to bring about meaningful change in the district.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 25, 2026
World.content:
Two UN Peacekeepers Killed in South Sudan Ambush

Two UN peacekeepers have been killed and seven others injured after unidentified gunmen ambushed a UNMISS patrol in South Sudan's eastern Jonglei state. The injured include three peacekeepers, two national police officers and two civilian staff. UNMISS chief Anita Kiki Gbeho condemned the attack and called for a prompt investigation, warning that attacks on peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. The incident comes as renewed violence puts South Sudan's fragile peace process under increasing strain. The country remains one of the world's most dangerous places for aid workers, with at least 36 humanitarian workers killed since January.

Prince Harry Steps Down from African Parks Board



Prince Harry has stepped down from the board of African Parks, an African wildlife charity he supported for 10 years. However, he remains a supporter of its conservation mission. His departure follows an independent investigation into allegations that rangers managed and funded by the organisation committed human rights abuses, including beatings, rape and torture, against indigenous people in Congo-Brazzaville. African Parks admitted the abuses last year and said it had since strengthened its safeguarding measures and governance. Harry's exit comes as he and Meghan prepare to relocate with their children from California to the UK.

Kagame Slams 'One-Sided' US Sanctions Over DR Congo Conflict

Rwandan President Paul Kagame has criticised US sanctions imposed over Rwanda's alleged involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. He said that they add to existing problems without addressing the root causes of the crisis. The US sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Force and four senior commanders in March, accusing them of supporting AFC/M23. Kigali described the measures as one-sided. Kagame said international pressure should also address the role of the FDLR, the Congolese government and other actors, arguing that the conflict cannot be blamed solely on Rwanda. He said Rwanda would continue pursuing peace while taking measures it considers necessary to protect its security.

Former DP Gachagua Vows to Contest 2027 Presidential Election

Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has said that his impeachment does not automatically prevent him from contesting the 2027 presidential election. Gachagua is challenging the decision in the Court of Appeal and potentially the Supreme Court. Gachagua argued that the High Court acknowledged his right to a fair hearing was violated. However, they still upheld his removal from office, which he called a constitutional "absurdity". Gachagua insists he remains a presidential contender, declaring that he is not a "kingmaker" but a potential candidate himself. He said that his opposition to President William Ruto is driven by concerns over governance rather than personal bitterness.

Close 

Tanzania Commission Begins Probe Into Election Violence

The Presidential Commission of Inquiry into the Individuals Involved in Violence and Violations of the Law during and after the October 2025 General Election has officially begun preparations to investigate those responsible. Commission chairperson retired Court of Appeal Judge Shaban Ali Lila said it will collect evidence from the public and other stakeholders. He said the commission would receive oral testimony, examine documents, and visit locations identified as connected to the incidents under investigation. The commission, established by President Samia Suluhu Hassan, will assess the evidence in accordance with Tanzanian laws and regulations.

US Seeks Wider UN Arms Embargo on Sudan

The United States has proposed expanding the UN arms embargo on Darfur to cover all of Sudan, as the country's civil war enters its fourth year. US Envoy Massad Boulos told the UN Security Council that weapons and financial support from outside powers were fuelling the conflict and proposed including drones and related technology under the embargo, as well as increasing monitoring. Sudan has backed a technical extension of the existing embargo but warned against measures that could weaken its army. Russia has expressed concerns about expanding the sanctions. The war between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions, with Darfur among the areas worst affected by violence.

World.title: South Africa: Businessman Seeks Bail in Trafficking Case - South African News Briefs - August 25, 2026
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal Businessman Seeks Bail in Trafficking Case

A KwaZulu-Natal businessman accused of human trafficking and sexual exploitation is set to apply for bail at the Durban Magistrates Court, reports EWN. The 65-year-old, whose identity is protected by law, was arrested by the Hawks. He is accused of being the ringleader of a trafficking operation in which four women were allegedly lured from Johannesburg to Durban with promises of sales jobs before being forced into prostitution and pornography. His alleged accomplice, a 48-year-old man, is also expected in court. The businessman has also been linked to senior police officers and politicians through testimony at the Madlanga Commission.

Two Killed, 12 Injured in Eastern Cape Crash



Two people have been killed and 12 others injured in a collision involving a car and a minibus taxi in Duncan Village in KuGompo City, Eastern Cape, reports SABC News. The crash occurred as the two vehicles were travelling in opposite directions. The provincial Transport Department has said that reckless and negligent driving is suspected to have contributed to the collision. The injured passengers were taken to Cecilia Makiwane and Frere hospitals, while a case of culpable homicide has been opened at Duncan Village SAPS.

Limpopo Lawyer, Cop Husband Seek Bail in R4m Fraud Case

A Limpopo lawyer and her Tshwane Metro Police officer husband are set to continue their bail application over allegations that they defrauded three deceased estates of more than R4 million, reports EWN. Charlotte Tibana, who runs a law firm in Polokwane, is accused of unlawfully transferring money from trust accounts. Acting as executor, while Peter "Gagash" Nonyane is alleged to have been involved in the fraud. The State is opposing bail and has expanded the allegations from an initial R1.75 million to more than R4 million. Tibana faces three counts of fraud and two of money laundering. Nonyane faces two counts each of fraud and money laundering. Both deny the allegations.
